title: Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Implementation

questions.question: Who should review and approve system deliverables as they are defined and accomplished, to ensure the successful completion and implementation of a new business system application?

options.D: Quality assurance (QA) staff

questions.correct_explanation: User management assumes ownership of the project and resulting system, allocates qualified representatives to the team, and actively participates in system requirements definition, acceptance testing and user training. User management should review and approve system deliverables as they are defined and accomplished or implemented.

wrong_explanations.B: A project steering committee provides overall direction, ensures appropriate representation of the major stakeholders in the project's outcome, reviews project progress regularly and holds emergency meetings when required. A project steering committee is ultimately responsible for all deliverables, project costs and schedules.
wrong_explanations.C: Senior management demonstrates commitment to the project and approves the necessary resources to complete the project. This commitment from senior management helps to ensure involvement by those who are needed to complete the project.
wrong_explanations.D: Quality assurance (QA) staff review results and deliverables within each phase, and, at the end of each phase, confirm compliance with standards and requirements. The timing of reviews depends on the system development life cycle (SDLC), the impact of potential deviation methodology used, the structure and magnitude of the system, and the impact of potential deviation.

tips: Trap is B 'project steering committee' — provides oversight and direction, but doesn't review individual deliverables for fitness.
Trap is C 'senior management' — approves resources and major milestones, but doesn't review deliverables operationally.
Trap is D 'QA staff' — reviews against quality standards, but the user owns whether the system meets THEIR needs.
User management owns the system being built. They alone can confirm 'this deliverable matches what we asked for'.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST helps to prioritize project activities and determine the time line for a project?

options.D: Function point analysis

questions.correct_explanation: The PERT method works on the principle of obtaining project timelines based on project events for three likely scenarios-worst, best and normal. The timeline is calculated by a predefined formula and identifies the critical path, which identifies the key activities that must be prioritized.

wrong_explanations.A: A Gantt chart is a simple project management tool which typically shows the timeline, status, and responsible person for each task in the project. It helps with the prioritization requirement, but it is not as effective as program evaluation review technique (PERT).
wrong_explanations.B: Earned value analysis is a technique to track project cost versus project deliverables but does not assist in prioritizing tasks. It provides better clarity and control of the activities involved and enables project managers to respond to issues early.
wrong_explanations.D: Function point analysis is a standardized method used commonly as an estimation technique in software engineering. It measures the complexity of input and output and does not help to prioritize project activities.

tips: Trap is A 'Gantt chart' — visualizes the schedule but doesn't help PRIORITIZE based on dependency criticality.
Trap is B 'earned value analysis' — measures progress vs plan, doesn't determine the timeline.
Trap is D 'function point analysis' — sizes the work, doesn't sequence it.
PERT identifies the critical path — the sequence of dependent activities determining minimum project duration. That's how priority and timeline get set.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing a series of completed projects finds that the implemented functionality often exceeded requirements and most of the projects ran significantly over budget. Which of these areas of the organization's project management process is the MOST likely cause of this issue?

options.D: Project procurement management

questions.correct_explanation: Because the implemented functionality is greater than what was required, the most likely cause of the budget issue is failure to effectively manage project scope. Project scope management is defined as the processes required to ensure that the project includes all of the required work, and only the required work, to complete the project.

wrong_explanations.B: Project time management is defined as the processes required to ensure timely completion of the project. The issue noted in the question does not mention whether projects were completed on time, so this is not the most likely cause.
wrong_explanations.C: Project risk management is defined as the processes concerned with identifying, analyzing and responding to project risk. Although the budget overruns mentioned above represent one form of project risk, they appear to be caused by implementing too much functionality, which relates more directly to project scope.
wrong_explanations.D: Project procurement management is defined as the processes required to acquire goods and services from outside the performing organization. Although purchasing goods and services that are too expensive can cause budget overruns, in this case, the key to the question is that implemented functionality is greater than what was required, which is more likely related to project scope.

tips: Trap is B 'time management' — the time issue is a SYMPTOM; the cause is functionality exceeding requirements.
Trap is C 'risk management' — should have caught the scope expansion but isn't the root cause discipline.
Trap is D 'procurement' — unrelated to scope creep.
Implementing functionality beyond requirements = scope expansion = scope management failure. Time and cost overruns are downstream consequences.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing the software development process for an organization. Which of the following functions are appropriate for the end users to perform?

options.D: Performance tuning

questions.correct_explanation: A user can test program output by checking the program input and comparing it with the system output. This task, although usually done by the programmer, can also be done effectively by the user.

wrong_explanations.B: System configuration is usually too technical to be accomplished by a user and this situation can create security issues and introduce a separation of duties issue.
wrong_explanations.C: Program logic specification is a very technical task that is normally performed by a programmer. A user performing this task can introduce a separation of duties issue.
wrong_explanations.D: Performance tuning also requires high levels of technical skill and cannot be effectively accomplished by a user. A user performing this task can introduce a separation of duties issue.

tips: Trap is B 'system configuration' — too technical for end users; potential security risk.
Trap is C 'program logic specification' — programmer's territory; users can't validate logic, only outcomes.
Trap is D 'performance tuning' — technical, requires deep system knowledge.
End users excel at output testing because they know what 'right' looks like for their job. Comparing inputs to expected outputs is squarely within user competence.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing system development for a health care organization with two application environments-production and test. During an interview, the auditor notes that production data are used in the test environment to test program changes. What is the MOST significant potential risk from this situation?

options.A: The test environment may not have adequate controls to ensure data accuracy.
options.B: The test environment may produce inaccurate results due to use of production data.
options.C: Hardware in the test environment may not be identical to the production environment.
options.D: The test environment may not have adequate access controls implemented to ensure data confidentiality.

questions.correct_explanation: In many cases, the test environment is not configured with the same access controls that are enabled in the production environment. For example, programmers may have privileged access to the test environment (for testing purposes), but not to the production environment. If the test environment does not have adequate access control, the production data are subject to risk of unauthorized access and/or data disclosure. This is the most significant risk of the choices listed and is especially important in a health care organization where patient data confidentiality is critical and privacy laws in many countries impose strict penalties on misuse of these data.

wrong_explanations.A: The accuracy of data used in the test environment is not of significant concern if these data are representative of the production environment.
wrong_explanations.B: Using production data in the test environment does not cause test results to be inaccurate; it has the opposite effect. Using production data improves the accuracy of testing processes, because the data most closely mirrors the production environment. Despite this, the risk of data disclosure or unauthorized access in the test environment is significant; therefore, production data should not be used in the test environment.
wrong_explanations.C: Hardware in the test environment should mirror the production environment to ensure that testing is reliable. However, this does not relate to the risk of using live data in a test environment and is not the correct answer.

tips: Trap is A 'data accuracy controls' — production data is already accurate.
Trap is B 'inaccurate test results' — production data tends to make tests MORE realistic, not less.
Trap is C 'hardware not identical' — environment concern, not data concern.

Production data in a test environment with weaker access controls = confidentiality breach risk. Programmers may have test environment access they wouldn't have in production — exposing sensitive data.

questions.question: The information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing a recently completed conversion to a new enterprise resource planning system. In the final stage of the conversion process, the organization ran the old and new systems in parallel for 30 days before allowing the new system to run on its own. What is the MOST significant advantage to the organization by using this strategy?

options.A: Significant cost savings over other testing approaches
options.B: Assurance that new, faster hardware is compatible with the new system
options.C: Assurance that the new system meets functional requirements
options.D: Increased resiliency during the parallel processing time

questions.correct_explanation: Parallel operation provides a high level of assurance that the new system functions properly compared to the old system, and therefore, the new system meets its functional requirements. This is the safest form of system conversion testing because, if the new system fails, the old system is still available for production use. In addition, this form of testing allows the application developers and administrators to simultaneously run operational tasks (e.g., batch jobs and backups) on both systems, to ensure that the new system is reliable before unplugging the old system.

wrong_explanations.A: Parallel operation is generally expensive and does not provide a cost savings over most other testing approaches. In many cases, parallel operation is the most expensive form of system testing due to the need for dual data entry, dual sets of hardware, dual maintenance and dual backups. Parallel operation is twice the amount of work as running a production system and, therefore, costs more time and money.
wrong_explanations.B: Hardware compatibility should be determined and tested much earlier in the conversion project and is not an advantage of parallel operation. Compatibility is generally determined based on the application's published specifications and on system testing in a lab environment. Parallel operation is designed to test the application's effectiveness and integrity of application data, not hardware compatibility. In general, hardware compatibility relates more to the operating system level than to a particular application. Although new hardware in a system conversion must be tested under a real production load, this can be done without parallel systems.
wrong_explanations.D: Increased resiliency during parallel processing is a legitimate outcome from this scenario, but the advantage it provides is temporary and minor, so this is not the correct answer.

tips: Trap is A 'cost savings' — parallel running is EXPENSIVE (running two systems for 30 days).
Trap is B 'hardware compatibility' — verified earlier in the project, not by parallel run.
Trap is D 'increased resiliency' — true side effect but not the primary advantage of parallel running.
Parallel running compares new system output to known-good old system output. That's the strongest assurance the new system works correctly — by direct comparison.

questions.question: What kind of software application testing is considered the final stage of testing and typically includes users outside of the development team?

options.D: Beta testing

questions.correct_explanation: Beta testing is the final stage of testing and typically includes users outside of the development area. Beta testing is a form of user acceptance testing and generally involves a limited number of users who are external to the development effort.

wrong_explanations.A: Alpha testing is the testing stage just before beta testing. Alpha testing is typically performed by programmers and business analysts, instead of users. Alpha testing is used to identify bugs or glitches that can be fixed before beta testing begins with external users.
wrong_explanations.B: White box testing is performed much earlier in the software development life cycle than alpha or beta testing. White box testing is used to assess the effectiveness of software program logic, where test data are used to determine procedural accuracy of the programs being tested. This testing stage determines if the program operates the way it is supposed to at a functional level. White box testing does not typically involve external users.
wrong_explanations.C: Regression testing is the process of re-running a portion of a test scenario to ensure that changes or corrections have not introduced more errors (i.e., the same tests are run after multiple successive program changes to ensure that the fix for one problem did not break another part of the program). Regression testing is not the last stage of testing and does not typically involve external users.

tips: Trap is A 'alpha testing' — early-stage testing, internal only.
Trap is B 'white box testing' — code-aware testing during development, not user testing.
Trap is C 'regression testing' — validates that fixes didn't break other things, not user-facing.
Beta testing = late-stage, real users in real conditions. Last verification before release.

questions.question: During which phase of software application testing should an organization perform the testing of architectural design?

options.D: Unit testing

questions.correct_explanation: Integration testing evaluates the connection of two or more components that pass information from one area to another. The objective is to use unit-tested modules, thus building an integrated structure according to the design.

wrong_explanations.A: Acceptance testing determines whether the solution meets the requirements of the business and is performed after system staff has completed the initial system test. This testing includes quality assurance testing and user acceptance testing, although not combined.
wrong_explanations.B: System testing relates a series of tests by the test team or system maintenance staff to ensure that the modified program interacts correctly with other components. System testing references the functional requirements of the system.
wrong_explanations.D: Unit testing references the detailed design of the system and uses a set of cases that focus on the control structure of the procedural design to ensure that the internal operation of the program performs according to specification.

tips: Trap is A 'acceptance testing' — final user-facing test, not architectural.
Trap is B 'system testing' — full system integration, but architectural design is tested earlier.
Trap is D 'unit testing' — module-level, doesn't test architecture.
Integration testing exercises the architectural design — how components connect. Unit-tested modules combined according to design = integration test.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of an integrated test facility?

options.A: It uses actual master files or dummies, and the information systems (IS) auditor does not have to review the source of the transaction.
options.B: Periodic testing does not require separate test processes.
options.C: It validates application systems and ensures the correct operation of the system.
options.D: The need to prepare test data is eliminated.

questions.correct_explanation: An ITF creates a fictitious entity in the database to process test transactions simultaneously with live input. Its advantage is that periodic testing does not require separate test processes. Careful planning is necessary, and test data must be isolated from production data.

wrong_explanations.A: The integrated test facility (ITF) tests a test transaction as if it were a real transaction and validates that transaction processing is being done correctly. It is not related to reviewing the source of a transaction.
wrong_explanations.C: An ITF does validate the correct operation of a transaction in an application, but it does not ensure that a system is being operated correctly.
wrong_explanations.D: The ITF is based on the integration of test data into the normal process flow, so test data is still required.

tips: ITF runs test transactions WITH live data using a fictitious entity. Tests can run anytime without separate test infrastructure.
Trap is A 'no need to review transaction source' — false; auditor still needs source verification.
Trap is C 'validates application AND ensures correct operation' — too broad; ITF is a specific testing approach, not a guarantee.
Trap is D 'no test data needed' — false; test transactions are still required, just integrated with live processing.

questions.question: An organization is replacing a payroll program that it developed in-house, with the relevant subsystem of a commercial enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. Which of the following represents the HIGHEST potential risk?

options.A: Undocumented approval of some project changes
options.B: Faulty migration of historical data from the old system to the new system
options.C: Incomplete testing of the standard functionality of the ERP subsystem
options.D: Duplication of existing payroll permissions on the new ERP subsystem

questions.correct_explanation: The most significant risk after a payroll system conversion is loss of data integrity resulting in the organization being unable to pay employees in a timely and accurate manner. Loss of data integrity can also result in incorrect records of past payments. As a result, maintaining data integrity and accuracy during migration is paramount.

wrong_explanations.A: Undocumented changes (leading to scope creep) are a risk, but the greatest risk is the loss of data integrity when migrating data from the old system to the new system.
wrong_explanations.C: A lack of testing is always a risk; however, in this case, the new payroll system is a subsystem of an existing commercially available (and therefore probably well-tested) system.
wrong_explanations.D: Setting up the new system, including access permissions and payroll data, always presents some level of risk; however, the greatest risk is related to the migration of data from the old system to the new system.

tips: Trap is A 'undocumented project change approvals' — process concern, recoverable.
Trap is C 'incomplete testing of standard functionality' — manageable through additional UAT.
Trap is D 'duplicating existing payroll permissions' — operational concern, configurable.
Faulty data migration in payroll = wrong paychecks. Direct human/financial/legal consequence. Highest-impact risk in the scenario.

questions.question: An enterprise is developing a strategy to upgrade to a newer version of its database software. Which of the following tasks can an information systems (IS) auditor perform without compromising the objectivity of the IS audit function?

options.A: Advise on the adoption of application controls to the new database software.
options.B: Provide future estimates of the licensing expenses to the project team.
options.C: Recommend to the project manager how to improve the efficiency of the migration.
options.D: Review the acceptance test case documentation before the tests are carried out.

questions.correct_explanation: The review of the test cases will facilitate the objective of a successful migration and ensure that proper testing is conducted. An IS auditor can advise about the completeness of the test cases.

wrong_explanations.A: Independence can be compromised if the information systems (IS) auditor advises on the adoption of specific application controls.
wrong_explanations.B: Independence can be compromised if the IS auditor were to audit the estimate of future expenses used to support a business case for management approval of the project.
wrong_explanations.C: Advising the project manager on how to increase the efficiency of the migration may compromise the IS auditor's independence.

tips: Trap is A 'advise on application controls adoption' — designing controls compromises auditor independence.
Trap is B 'provide future licensing estimates' — auditor doesn't do project budgeting.
Trap is C 'recommend efficiency improvements' — operational consulting, compromises independence.
Reviewing test case documentation is audit-appropriate: assess completeness without designing or operating controls. Stays within the audit role.

questions.question: During a postimplementation review, which of the following activities should be performed?

options.D: Updates of the state of enterprise architecture (EA) diagrams

questions.correct_explanation: Following implementation, a cost-benefit analysis or return on investment (ROI) should be reperformed to verify that the original business case benefits are delivered and business value is created.

wrong_explanations.A: User acceptance testing (UAT) supports the process of ensuring that the system is production ready and satisfies all documented requirements. User acceptance testing should be performed prior to the implementation (perhaps during the development phase), not after the implementation.
wrong_explanations.C: An audit trail is a detailed record of the activities on a database or system. The audit trail should be activated during the implementation of the application, not during the postimplementation review.
wrong_explanations.D: Although updating the enterprise architecture (EA) diagrams is a good practice, it is not normally part of a postimplementation review.

tips: Trap is A 'UAT' — happens before implementation, not during postimplementation review.
Trap is C 'activate audit trails' — should already be active; not a postimplementation activity.
Trap is D 'update EA diagrams' — documentation hygiene, not the primary postimplementation question.
Postimplementation review answers: did this investment deliver promised value? ROI analysis re-evaluates the original business case against actual outcomes.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST approach to ensure that sufficient test coverage will be achieved for a project with a strict end date and a fixed time to perform testing?

options.A: Requirements should be tested in terms of importance and frequency of use.
options.B: Test coverage should be restricted to functional requirements.
options.C: Automated tests should be performed using scripting.
options.D: The number of required test runs should be reduced by retesting only defect fixes.

questions.correct_explanation: This approach maximizes the usefulness of testing by concentrating on the most important aspects of the system and on the areas where defects represent the greatest risk to user acceptance. A further extension of this approach is to also consider the technical complexity of requirements because complexity tends to increase the likelihood of defects.

wrong_explanations.B: The problem with testing only functional requirements is that nonfunctional requirement areas, such as usability and security, which are important to the overall quality of the system, are ignored.
wrong_explanations.C: Increasing the efficiency of testing by automating test execution is a good idea. However, by itself, this approach does not ensure the appropriate targeting of test coverage and is not an effective alternative.
wrong_explanations.D: Retesting only defect fixes has a considerable risk that it will not detect instances in which defect fixes may have caused the system to regress (i.e., introduced errors in parts of the system that were previously working correctly). For this reason, it is a good practice to undertake formal regression testing after defect fixes have been implemented.

tips: Trap is B 'restrict to functional requirements' — ignores nonfunctional (performance, security, usability) which are equally important.
Trap is C 'automated tests with scripting' — useful tactically but doesn't ensure coverage of important areas.
Trap is D 'retest only defect fixes' — leaves untouched code untested; coverage gap.
Risk-based testing: use frequency and importance to allocate scarce test time to highest-risk requirements. Maximizes risk reduction per test hour.

questions.question: By evaluating application development projects against the capability maturity model, an information systems (IS) auditor should be able to verify that:

options.D: predictable software processes are followed.

questions.correct_explanation: By evaluating the organization's development projects against the CMM, an information systems (IS) auditor determines whether the development organization follows a stable, predictable software development process.

wrong_explanations.A: Although the likelihood of success should increase as the software processes mature toward the optimizing level, mature processes do not guarantee a reliable product.
wrong_explanations.B: The capability maturity model (CMM) does not evaluate technical processes such as programming efficiency.
wrong_explanations.C: The CMM does not evaluate security requirements or other application controls.

tips: Trap is A 'reliable products guaranteed' — too strong; CMM measures process, not product reliability.
Trap is B 'efficiency improved' — possible outcome, not what CMM measures.
Trap is C 'security designed' — separate concern from process maturity.
CMM evaluates whether the dev organization has STABLE, PREDICTABLE processes. That's the entire point: process maturity, not specific outcomes.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is performing a postimplementation review of an organization's system and identifies output errors within an accounting application. The IS auditor determines that this was caused by input errors. Which of the following controls should the IS auditor recommend to management?

options.D: Reconciliations

questions.correct_explanation: Processing controls should be implemented as close as possible to the point of data entry. Limit checks are one type of input validation check that provides a preventive control to ensure that invalid data cannot be entered, because values must fall within a predetermined limit.

wrong_explanations.A: A sample of transactions may be recalculated manually to ensure that processing is accomplishing the anticipated task. Recalculations are performed after the output phase.
wrong_explanations.C: Run-to-run totals provide the ability to verify data values through the stages of application processing. Run-to-run total verification ensures that data read into the computer are accepted and then applied to the updating process. Run-to-run totals are performed after the output phase.
wrong_explanations.D: Reconciliation of file totals should be performed on a routine basis. Reconciliations may be performed through the use of a manually maintained account, a file control record or an independent control file. Reconciliations are performed after the output phase.

tips: Trap is A/D 'recalculations / reconciliations' — detective controls; don't prevent input errors.
Trap is C 'run-to-run totals' — detect processing errors, not input errors.
Limit checks operate at input time, rejecting invalid values before they enter the system. Preventive control closest to the source.

questions.question: Due to a reorganization, a business application system will be extended to other departments. Which of the following should be of the GREATEST concern for an information systems (IS) auditor?

options.A: Process owners have not been identified.
options.B: The billing cost allocation method has not been determined.
options.D: A training program does not exist.

questions.correct_explanation: When one application is expanded to multiple departments, it is important to ensure the mapping between the process owner and system functions. The absence of a defined process owner may cause issues with monitoring or authorization controls.

wrong_explanations.B: Cost allocation is the method business owners use to calculate profitability for the purpose of financial reporting. The billing cost allocation method of application usage is ofless importance than identifying process owners.
wrong_explanations.C: The fact that multiple application owners exist is not a concern for an information systems (IS) auditor if process owners have been identified, because the process owners are responsible for the specific process.
wrong_explanations.D: The lack of a training program is only a minor concern for the IS auditor.

tips: Trap is B 'billing cost allocation' — financial concern, addressable post-rollout.
Trap is C 'multiple application owners' — common in shared apps; manageable through governance.
Trap is D 'no training program' — user adoption issue, addressable.
Without process owners, there's no accountability for operations, monitoring, or authorization decisions. Foundational governance gap that affects all departments.

questions.question: When auditing the proposed acquisition of a new computer system, an information systems (IS) auditor should FIRST ensure that:

options.A: a clear business case has been approved by management.
options.B: corporate security standards will be met.
options.C: users will be involved in the implementation plan.
options.D: the new system will meet all required user functionality.

questions.correct_explanation: The first concern of an information systems (IS) auditor is to ensure that the proposal meets the needs of the business. This should be established by a clear business case.

wrong_explanations.B: Compliance with security standards is essential, but it is too early in the procurement process for this to be an IS auditor's first concern.
wrong_explanations.C: Having users involved in the implementation process is essential, but it is too early in the procurement process for this to be an IS auditor's first concern.
wrong_explanations.D: Meeting the needs of the users is essential, and this should be included in the business case presented to management for approval.

tips: Trap is B 'security standards met' — checked later in the acquisition process.
Trap is C 'users involved in implementation' — implementation phase concern, not initial acquisition.
Trap is D 'meets all user functionality' — too broad; may not be required and may exceed budget.
Acquisition starts with a clear business case approved by management. Without that, the entire acquisition lacks business justification — everything else is moot.

questions.question: Which of the following types of a risk is MOST likely encountered in a software as a service (SaaS) environment?

options.B: Performance issues due to Internet delivery method
options.C: Higher cost due to software licensing requirements
options.D: Higher cost due to the need to update to compatible hardware

questions.correct_explanation: The risk that can be most likely encountered in a SaaS environment is speed and availability issues because SaaS relies on the Internet for connectivity.

wrong_explanations.A: Software as a service (SaaS) is provisioned on a usage basis and the number of users is monitored by the SaaS provider; therefore, there should be no risk of noncompliance with software license agreements.
wrong_explanations.C: The costs for a SaaS solution should be fixed as a part of the services contract and considered in the business case presented to management for approval of the solution.
wrong_explanations.D: The open design and Internet connectivity allow most SaaS to run on any type of hardware.

tips: Trap is A 'noncompliance with software licensing' — SaaS reduces this risk; vendor manages licensing.
Trap is C 'higher cost from licensing' — SaaS typically REDUCES total cost.
Trap is D 'higher cost for compatible hardware' — SaaS doesn't require hardware updates.
SaaS depends entirely on Internet connectivity. Performance and availability follow Internet quality, not the customer's local infrastructure. Most likely day-to-day risk.

questions.question: The most common reason for the failure of information systems to meet the needs of users is that:

options.B: the growth of system requirements was forecast inaccurately.
options.C: the hardware system limits the number of concurrent users.
options.D: user participation in defining the system's requirements was inadequate.

questions.correct_explanation: Lack of adequate user involvement, especially in the system's requirements phase, usually results in a system that does not fully or adequately address the needs of the user. Only users can define what their needs are and, therefore, what the system should accomplish.

wrong_explanations.A: Although changing user needs influences the success or failure of many projects, the core problem is usually a lack of getting the initial requirements correct at the beginning of the project.
wrong_explanations.B: Projects may fail as the needs of the users increase; however, this can be mitigated through better change control procedures.
wrong_explanations.C: Rarely do hardware limitations affect the usability of the project if the requirements were correctly documented at the beginning of the project.

tips: Trap is A 'changing user needs' — manageable through change control; not the most common cause.
Trap is B 'inaccurate growth forecast' — capacity issue, addressable through scaling.
Trap is C 'hardware concurrency limits' — technical, addressable.
Inadequate user participation in requirements = systems built to assumed needs, not actual needs. Most fundamental and most common failure mode.

questions.question: Many IT projects experience problems because the development time and/or resource requirements are underestimated. Which of the following techniques provides the GREATEST assistance in developing an estimate of project duration?

options.D: Object-oriented system development

questions.correct_explanation: The program evaluation review technique (PERT) method works on the principle of obtaining project timelines based on project events for three likely scenarios-worst, best and normal. The timeline is calculated by a predefined formula and identifies the critical path, which identifies the key activities that must be prioritized. A PERT chart helps determine project duration after all the activities and the work involved with those activities are known.

wrong_explanations.A: Function point analysis is a technique for determining the size of a development task based on the number of function points. Function points are factors such as inputs, outputs, inquiries and logical internal files. Although this helps determine the size of individual activities, it does not assist in determining project duration, because there are many overlapping tasks.
wrong_explanations.C: Rapid application development is a methodology that enables organizations to develop strategically important systems faster, while reducing development costs and maintaining quality.
wrong_explanations.D: Object-oriented design is an approach to systems development that proposes the use of system objects to build new systems and rebuild old ones. An important goal of object-oriented development is to change the nature of traditional software development from designing and writing models from scratch to building systems through the assembly of reusable software objects. Object-oriented system development is the process of solution specification and modeling but does not assist in calculating project duration.

tips: Trap is A 'function point analysis' — sizes the work, doesn't directly estimate duration.
Trap is C 'rapid application development' — methodology, doesn't estimate.
Trap is D 'object-oriented system development' — design approach, doesn't estimate.
PERT estimates duration using best/worst/normal scenarios. Specifically designed for project duration estimation under uncertainty.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing IT projects for a large enterprise and wants to determine whether the IT projects undertaken in a given year are those which have been assigned the highest priority by the business and which will generate the greatest business value. Which of the following is MOST relevant?

options.D: Project management body of knowledge

questions.correct_explanation: Portfolio management is designed to assist in the definition, prioritization, approval and running of a set of projects within a given organization. These tools offer data capture, workflow and scenario planning functionality, which can help identify the optimum set of projects (from the full set of ideas) to take forward within a given budget.

wrong_explanations.A: A capability maturity model (CMM) is a means of assessing the relative maturity of the IT processes within an organization, running from Level O (Incomplete-processes are not implemented or fail to achieve their purpose) to Level 5 (Optimizing-metrics are defined and measured, and continuous improvement techniques are in place). It does not help determine the optimal portfolio of capital projects, because it assesses the maturity of the processes.
wrong_explanations.C: A configuration management database, which stores the configuration details for an organization's IT systems, is an important tool for IT service delivery and, in particular, change management. A configuration management database may provide information that would influence the prioritization of projects but is not designed for that purpose.
wrong_explanations.D: The project management body of knowledge is a methodology for the management and delivery of projects. It offers no specific guidance or assistance for optimizing a project portfolio.

tips: Trap is A 'CMM' — assesses process maturity, doesn't help select projects.
Trap is C 'configuration management' — controls software/hardware versions, not project selection.
Trap is D 'PMBOK' — body of knowledge for managing projects, not selecting them.
Portfolio management is purpose-built for project prioritization across the org — comparing initiatives by business value and risk. That's what enables strategic project selection.

questions.question: The reason for establishing a stop or freezing point on the design of a new system is to:

options.A: prevent further changes to a project in process.
options.B: indicate the point at which the design is to be completed.
options.C: require that changes after that point be evaluated for cost-effectiveness.
options.D: provide the project management team with more control over the project design.

questions.correct_explanation: Projects often tend to expand, especially during the requirements definition phase. This expansion often grows to a point where the originally anticipated cost benefits are diminished because the cost of the project has increased. When this occurs, it is recommended that the project be stopped or frozen to allow a review of all the cost benefits and the payback period.

wrong_explanations.A: The stop point is intended to provide greater control over changes but not to prevent them.
wrong_explanations.B: The stop point is used for project control but not to create an artificial fixed point that requires the design of the project to cease.
wrong_explanations.D: A stop point is used to control requirements, not project design.

tips: Trap is A 'prevent further changes' — too restrictive; changes are valuable when justified.
Trap is B 'design completion point' — descriptive, not the rationale for the freeze.
Trap is D 'project management control' — outcome but not the primary purpose.
Stop point exists to FORCE cost-benefit evaluation of late changes. Without it, scope creep destroys the original business case.

questions.question: Change control for business application systems being developed using prototyping can be complicated by the:

options.B: rapid pace of modifications in requirements and design.
options.D: lack of integrated tools.

questions.correct_explanation: Changes in requirements and design happen so quickly that they are seldom documented or approved.

wrong_explanations.A: A characteristic of prototyping is its iterative nature, but it does not have an adverse effect on change control.
wrong_explanations.C: A characteristic of prototyping is its emphasis on reports and screens, but it does not have an adverse effect on change control.
wrong_explanations.D: Lack of integrated tools is a characteristic of prototyping, but it does not have an adverse effect on change control.

tips: Trap is A 'iterative nature' — characteristic of prototyping, not the change-control complication.
Trap is C 'emphasis on reports and screens' — focus area, not change-control issue.
Trap is D 'lack of integrated tools' — tooling gap, addressable.
Prototyping moves fast — requirements and design change session by session. Documentation and approval can't keep up, undermining traditional change control.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor performing a review of a major software development project finds that it is on schedule and under budget even though the software developers have worked considerable amounts of unplanned overtime. The IS auditor should:

options.A: conclude that the project is progressing as planned because dates are being met.
options.B: question the project manager further to identify whether overtime costs are being tracked accurately.
options.C: conclude that the programmers are intentionally working slowly to earn extra overtime pay.
options.D: investigate further to determine whether the project plan may not be accurate.

questions.correct_explanation: Although the dates on which key projects are completed are important, there may be issues with the project plan if an extraordinary amount of unplanned overtime is required to meet those dates. In most cases, the project plan is based on a certain number of hours, and requiring programmers to work considerable overtime is not a good practice. Although overtime costs may be an indicator that something is wrong with the plan, in many organizations, the programming staff may be salaried, so overtime costs may not be directly recorded.

wrong_explanations.A: Although the project is on time and budget, there may be problems with the project plan because considerable amounts of unplanned overtime have been required.
wrong_explanations.B: There is a possibility that the project manager has hidden some costs to make the project look better; however, the real problem may be with whether the project plan is realistic, not just the accounting.
wrong_explanations.C: It is possible that the programmers are trying to take advantage of the time system, but if the overtime has been required to keep the project on track, it is more likely that the timelines and expectations of the project are unrealistic.

tips: Trap is A 'project progressing as planned' — superficially true (on time, under budget) but ignores team strain.
Trap is B 'overtime cost tracking' — accounting concern, not project plan concern.
Trap is C 'programmers slow to earn overtime' — unfair speculation about staff.
Massive unplanned overtime = the project plan was wrong (under-estimated). The plan is meeting deadlines through team burnout, not realistic scheduling. Investigate.

questions.question: A project development team is considering using production data for its test deck. The team removed sensitive data elements before loading it into the test environment. Which of the following additional concerns should an information systems (IS) auditor have with this practice?

options.A: Not all functionality will be tested.
options.B: Production data are introduced into the test environment.
options.D: The project may run over budget.

questions.correct_explanation: A primary risk of using production data in a test deck is that not all transactions or functionality may be tested if there are no data that meet the requirement.

wrong_explanations.B: The presence of production data in a test environment is not a concern if the sensitive elements have been scrubbed.
wrong_explanations.C: Creation of a test deck from production data does not require specialized knowledge, so this is not a concern.
wrong_explanations.D: The risk of a project running over budget is always a concern, but it is not related to the practice of using production data in a test environment.

tips: Trap is B 'production data introduced' — already addressed (sensitive data was scrubbed).
Trap is C 'specialized training' — operational concern, not test data concern.
Trap is D 'over budget' — generic project risk, not test deck specific.
Production data covers normal cases but may MISS edge cases, error conditions, and rare scenarios. Test functionality won't be fully exercised.

questions.question: Which of the following considerations is the MOST important while evaluating a business case for the acquisition of a new accounting application?

options.A: Total cost of ownership of the application
options.C: Return on investment (ROI) for the enterprise
options.D: The cost and complexity of security requirements

questions.correct_explanation: The proposed ROI benefits, and targets or metrics that can be measured, are the most important aspects of a business case. While reviewing the business case, it should be verified that the proposed ROI is achievable, does not make unreasonable assumptions and can be measured for success. (Benefits realization should look beyond project cycles to longer-term cycles that consider the total benefits and total costs throughout the life of the new system.)

wrong_explanations.A: Total cost of ownership of the application is important to understand the resource and budget requirements in the short and long term; however, decisions should be based on benefits realization from this investment. Therefore, return on investment (ROI) is the most important consideration.
wrong_explanations.B: The resources required for implementation of the application are an important consideration; however, decisions should be based on benefits realization from this investment. Therefore, ROI should be carefully considered.
wrong_explanations.D: The cost and complexity of security requirements are important considerations, but they need to be weighed against the proposed benefits of the application. Therefore, ROI is more important.

tips: Trap is A 'TCO' — important but a SUBSET of the ROI calculation.
Trap is B 'resources for implementation' — input to the cost side, not the full picture.
Trap is D 'security cost and complexity' — one cost component.
Business case = ROI = full benefit/cost picture. ROI is what justifies the acquisition; everything else is an input to ROI.

questions.question: The development of an application has been outsourced to an offshore vendor. Which of the following should be of GREATEST concern to an information systems (IS) auditor?

options.A: The right to audit clause was not included in the contract.
options.B: The business case was not established.
options.C: There was no source code escrow agreement.
options.D: The contract does not cover change management procedures.

questions.correct_explanation: Because the business case was not established, it is likely that the business rationale, risk and risk mitigation strategies for outsourcing the application development were not fully evaluated and the appropriate information was not provided to senior management for formal approval. This situation presents the biggest risk to the organization.

wrong_explanations.A: The lack of the right to audit clause presents a risk to the organization; however, the risk is not as consequential as the lack of a business case.
wrong_explanations.C: If the source code is held by the provider and not provided to the organization, the lack of source code escrow presents a risk to the organization; however, the risk is not as consequential as the lack of a business case.
wrong_explanations.D: The lack of change management procedures presents a risk to the organization, especially with the possibility of extraordinary charges for any required changes; however, the risk is not as consequential as the lack of a business case.

tips: Trap is A 'no right-to-audit clause' — concerning but addressable through other assurance mechanisms.
Trap is C 'no source code escrow' — addressable through contractual update.
Trap is D 'no change management coverage' — operational concern, can be added to contract.
No business case = the outsourcing decision wasn't strategically evaluated. Risk, value, alternatives, and exit strategies were never assessed. Foundational governance failure.

questions.question: Before implementing controls in a newly developed system, management should PRIMARILY ensure that the controls:

options.A: satisfy a requirement in addressing a risk.
options.C: are based on a minimized cost analysis.
options.D: are detective or corrective.

questions.correct_explanation: The purpose of a control is to mitigate a risk; therefore, the primary consideration when selecting a control is that it effectively mitigates an identified risk. When designing controls, it is necessary to consider all the aspects in the presented options. In an ideal situation, controls that address all these aspects are the best controls. Realistically, it may not be possible to design them all and the cost may be prohibitive; therefore, it is necessary to consider the controls that are related primarily to the treatment of existing risk in the organization.

wrong_explanations.B: Controls often affect productivity and performance; however, this must be balanced against the benefit obtained from the implementation of the control.
wrong_explanations.C: The most important reason for a control is to mitigate a risk-and the selection of a control is usually based on a cost-benefit analysis, not on selecting just the least expensive control.
wrong_explanations.D: A good control environment includes preventive, detective and corrective controls.

tips: Trap is B 'don't reduce productivity' — operational concern, secondary to risk mitigation purpose.
Trap is C 'minimized cost analysis' — backwards; controls should match risk, not minimize cost.
Trap is D 'detective or corrective' — false dichotomy; preventive controls are also valid.
Controls exist to mitigate identified RISK. Controls without a corresponding risk are wasteful; controls misaligned to risk are ineffective. Risk drives the requirement.

questions.question: Information for detecting unauthorized input from a user workstation is BEST provided by the:

options.D: user error report.

questions.correct_explanation: The transaction journal records all transaction activity, which then can be compared to the authorized source documents to identify any unauthorized input.

wrong_explanations.A: A console log printout is not the best source because it does not record activity from a specific terminal.
wrong_explanations.C: An automated suspense file listing lists only transaction activity where an edit error occurred.
wrong_explanations.D: The user error report lists only input that resulted in an edit error and does not record improper user input.

tips: Trap is A 'console log' — system-level, doesn't capture user transaction details.
Trap is C 'automated suspense file' — captures errors only, misses successful unauthorized input.
Trap is D 'user error report' — captures user-reported errors, not unauthorized actions.
Transaction journal captures every transaction with user attribution. Comparing journal entries to authorized sources surfaces unauthorized inputs.

questions.question: Which of the following has the MOST significant impact on the success of an application system implementation?

options.D: Software reengineering technique

questions.correct_explanation: The overall organizational environment has the most significant impact on the success of application systems implemented. This includes the alignment between IT and the business, the maturity of the development processes and the use of change control and other project management tools.

wrong_explanations.A: The prototyping application development technique reduces the time to deploy systems primarily by using faster development tools that allow a user to see a high-level view of the workings of the proposed system within a short period of time. The use of any one development methodology has a limited impact on the success of the project.
wrong_explanations.B: Compliance with applicable external requirements has an impact on the implementation success, but the impact is not as significant as the impact of the overall organizational environment.
wrong_explanations.D: The software reengineering technique is a process of updating an existing system by extracting and reusing design and program components. This is used to support major changes in the way an organization operates. Its impact on the success of the application systems that are implemented is small compared with the impact of the overall organizational environment.

tips: Trap is A 'prototyping methodology' — one factor, but methodology choice can succeed in good environments and fail in bad ones.
Trap is B 'external compliance' — important but doesn't drive overall success.
Trap is D 'software reengineering' — technique, not environment.
Organizational environment includes: business-IT alignment, process maturity, change control discipline, governance. Same project in different environments has wildly different outcomes.

questions.question: The editing/validation of data entered at a remote site is performed MOST effectively at the:

options.A: central processing site after running the application system.
options.B: central processing site during the running of the application system.
options.C: remote processing site after transmission of the data to the central processing site.
options.D: remote processing site prior to transmission of the data to the central processing site.

questions.correct_explanation: It is important that the data entered from a remote site are edited and validated prior to transmission to the central processing site.

wrong_explanations.A: Due to the risk of errors being introduced during transmission to the central processing site, it is a good practice to re-validate the data after receiving them at the central processing site. However, this is not the most efficient method, because invalid data could have been transmitted and processed.
wrong_explanations.B: Due to the risk of errors being introduced during transmission to the central processing site, it is a good practice to re-validate the data after receiving them at the central processing site. However, this is not the most efficient method, because invalid data could have been transmitted and processed at the central site.
wrong_explanations.C: To validate the data after they have been transmitted is not a valid control.

tips: Trap is A/B 'central site after / during application run' — already past the cost of bad transmission; data quality should be enforced earlier.
Trap is C 'remote site after transmission' — paradoxical; if you're going to validate at the remote site, do it BEFORE wasting bandwidth.
Validate at the source, before transmission. Catches errors with minimum cost — no wasted bandwidth, no central-site processing of bad data, no later cleanup.

questions.question: The MAJOR consideration for an information systems (IS) auditor reviewing an organization's IT project portfolio is the:

options.D: investment plan.

questions.correct_explanation: One of the most important determining factors for which projects get funded is how well a project meets an organization's strategic objectives. Portfolio management takes a holistic view of a company's overall IT strategy. IT strategy should be aligned with the business strategy and, hence, reviewing the business plan should be the major consideration.

wrong_explanations.A: The IT budget is important to ensure that the resources are being used in the best manner, but this is secondary to the importance of reviewing the business plan.
wrong_explanations.B: The existing IT environment is important and used to determine gap analysis but is secondary to the importance of reviewing the business plan.
wrong_explanations.D: The investment plan is important to set out project priorities, but secondary to the importance of reviewing the business plan.

tips: Trap is A/D 'IT budget / investment plan' — financial constraints, derived from business plan.
Trap is B 'existing IT environment' — current state, doesn't drive future selection.
Project portfolio prioritization is a strategic exercise. The business plan is the ultimate filter — projects must serve business strategy first; budget and environment are constraints, not drivers.

questions.question: Regression testing is undertaken PRIMARILY to ensure that:

options.B: a new system can operate in the target environment.
options.C: applicable development standards have been maintained.
options.D: applied changes have not introduced new errors.

questions.correct_explanation: Regression testing is used to test for the introduction of new errors in the system after changes have been applied.

wrong_explanations.A: Validation testing is used to testthe functionality of the system against detailed requirements to ensure that software construction is traceable to customer requirements.
wrong_explanations.B: Sociability testing is used to see whether the system can operate in the target environment without adverse impacts on the existing systems.
wrong_explanations.C: Software quality assurance and code reviews are used to determine whether development standards are maintained.

tips: Trap is A 'meets customer requirements' — that's UAT or system testing.
Trap is B 'operate in target environment' — that's sociability/deployment testing.
Trap is C 'development standards maintained' — quality assurance, not regression.
Regression testing's specific job: verify that changes didn't BREAK previously-working functionality. Re-running prior tests catches new errors introduced by changes.

questions.question: A proposed transaction processing application will have many data capture sources and outputs in paper and electronic form. To ensure that transactions are not lost during processing, an information systems (IS) auditor should recommend the inclusion of:

options.D: automated systems balancing.

questions.correct_explanation: Automated systems balancing is the best way to ensure that no transactions are lost because any imbalance between total inputs and total outputs is reported for investigation and correction.

wrong_explanations.A: Validation controls cancheck for required fields, formatand type ofdata, and other criteria that must be met before the data can be submitted to the server. This helps ensure that the data is accurate and complete and that the application can process them correctly. Input and output validation controls are, therefore, valid controls but do not detect and report lost transactions.
wrong_explanations.B: Internal credibility checks are valid controls to detect errors in processing but do not detect and report lost transactions.
wrong_explanations.C: A clerical procedure can be used to summarize and compare inputs and outputs; however, an automated process is less susceptible to error.

tips: Trap is A 'validation controls' — catch invalid input but don't track totals end-to-end.
Trap is B 'internal credibility checks' — sniff-test for plausibility, doesn't catch loss.
Trap is C 'clerical procedures' — manual, error-prone, doesn't scale.
Automated systems balancing: total inputs = total outputs. Discrepancy = lost transaction, automatically flagged for investigation. Best for multi-source/multi-format processing.

questions.question: Which of the following should be an information systems (IS) auditor's PRIMARY concern after discovering that the scope of an IS project has changed and an impact study has not been performed?

options.A: Time and cost implications caused by the change
options.B: Risk that regression tests will fail
options.C: Users not agreeing with the change
options.D: Project team not having the skills to make the necessary change

questions.correct_explanation: Any scope change might have an impact on the duration and cost of the project; that is the reason why an impact study is conducted and the client is informed of the potential impact on the schedule and cost.

wrong_explanations.B: A change in scope does not necessarily impact the risk that regression tests will fail.
wrong_explanations.C: An impact study does not determine whether users will agree with a change in scope.
wrong_explanations.D: Conducting an impact study can identify a lack of resources, such as the project team lacking the skills necessary to make the change; however, this is only part of the impact on the overall timelines and cost to the project due to the change.

tips: Trap is B 'regression test failures' — possible side effect, not the primary scope-change concern.
Trap is C 'users not agreeing' — adoption issue, secondary.
Trap is D 'team skills' — capability concern, secondary.
Scope changes shift duration and cost — that's why impact studies exist. Without one, the project commits to changes whose true cost is unknown.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing the software development capabilities of an organization that has adopted the agile methodology. The IS auditor would be the MOST concerned if:

options.A: certain project iterations produce proof-of-concept deliverables and unfinished code.
options.B: application features and development processes are not extensively documented.
options.C: software development teams continually re-plan each step of their major projects.
options.D: project managers do not manage project resources, leaving that to project team members.

questions.correct_explanation: The agile software development methodology is an iterative process where each iteration (sprint) produces functional code. If a development team is producing code for demonstration purposes, this is an issue because the following iterations of the project build on the code developed in the prior sprint.

wrong_explanations.B: One focus of agile methodology is to rely more on team knowledge and produce functional code quickly. These characteristics result in less extensive documentation or documentation embedded in the code itself.
wrong_explanations.C: After each sprint, agile development teams re-plan the project so that unfinished tasks are performed and resources can be reallocated as needed. The continual re-planning is a key component of agile development methodology.
wrong_explanations.D: The management of agile software development is different from conventional development approaches in that leaders act as facilitators and allow team members to determine how to manage their own resources to get each sprint completed. Because the team members are performing the work, they are in a good position to understand how much time/effort is required to complete a sprint.

tips: Trap is B 'features not extensively documented' — agile prefers minimal documentation; this is by design.
Trap is C 'continual re-planning' — agile core practice; iterative re-planning is expected.
Trap is D 'team manages own resources' — agile self-organization principle.
Agile's non-negotiable: each iteration produces SHIPPABLE code. Proof-of-concept and unfinished code violate the iteration principle and undermine agile's value proposition.

questions.question: Which of the following data validation edits is effective in detecting transposition and transcription errors?

options.D: Duplicate check

questions.correct_explanation: A check digit is a numeric value that is calculated mathematically and is appended to data to ensure that the original data have not been altered (e.g., an incorrect, but valid, value substituted for the original). This control is effective in detecting transposition and transcription errors.

wrong_explanations.A: A range check is checking data that matches a predetermined range of allowable values.
wrong_explanations.C: A validity check is programmed checking of the data validity in accordance with predetermined criteria.
wrong_explanations.D: In a duplicate check, new or fresh transactions are matched to those previously entered to ensure that they are not already in the system.

tips: Trap is A 'range check' — catches values outside allowed range, not order errors.
Trap is C 'validity check' — catches invalid values, not transposition.
Trap is D 'duplicate check' — catches duplicates, different problem.
Check digit is mathematically computed from the original digits. Transposing digits changes the computed value, exposing the error. Designed for transposition/transcription detection.

questions.question: Two months after a major application implementation, management, which assumes that the project went well, requests that an information systems (IS) auditor perform a review of the completed project. The IS auditor's PRIMARY focus should be to:

options.A: determine whether user feedback on the system has been documented.
options.B: assess whether the planned cost benefits are being measured, analyzed and reported.
options.C: review controls built into the system to assure that they are operating as designed.
options.D: review subsequent program change requests.

questions.correct_explanation: Because management is assuming that the implementation went well, the primary focus of the IS auditor is to test the controls built into the application to assure that they are functioning as designed.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor should check whether user feedback has been provided, but this is not the most important area for audit.
wrong_explanations.B: It is important to assess the effectiveness of the project; however, assuring that the production environment is adequately controlled after the implementation is of primary concern.
wrong_explanations.D: Reviewing change requests may be a good idea, but this is more important if the application is perceived to have a problem.

tips: Trap is A 'user feedback documented' — useful but doesn't validate system controls.
Trap is B 'cost benefits measured' — financial review, secondary in two months.
Trap is D 'subsequent change requests' — quality indicator, indirect.
Postimplementation control review tests whether built-in controls are working as designed. Management's 'went well' assumption needs INDEPENDENT verification — that's the auditor's value-add.

questions.question: Which of the following types of risk can result from inadequate software project baselining?

options.D: Inadequate controls

questions.correct_explanation: A software baseline is the cutoff point in the design and development of a system. Beyond this point, additional requirements or modifications to the scope must go through formal, strict procedures for approval based on a business cost-benefit analysis. Failure to adequately manage a system through baselining can result in uncontrolled changes in a project's scope and may incur time and budget overruns.

wrong_explanations.A: Sign-off delays may occur due to inadequate software baselining; however, these are most likely caused by scope creep.
wrong_explanations.B: Software integrity violations can be caused by hardware or software failures, malicious intrusions, or user errors. Software baselining does not help prevent software integrity violations.
wrong_explanations.D: Inadequate controls are most likely present in situations in which information security is not duly considered from the beginning of system development; they are not a risk that can be adequately addressed by software baselining.

tips: Trap is A 'sign-off delays' — process inconvenience, downstream of scope creep.
Trap is B 'software integrity violations' — different control problem.
Trap is D 'inadequate controls' — possible but indirect.
Without baselining, requirements continue evolving without formal cost-benefit evaluation. Result: SCOPE CREEP — the project keeps growing past its original justification.

questions.question: An organization implemented a distributed accounting system, and the information systems (IS) auditor is conducting a post-implementation review to provide assurance of the data integrity controls. Which of the following choices should the auditor perform FIRST?

options.D: Review the data flow diagram.

questions.correct_explanation: The information systems (IS) auditor should review the application data flow diagram to understand the flow of data within the application and to other systems. This will enable the IS auditor to evaluate the design and effectiveness of the data integrity controls.

wrong_explanations.A: The review of user access is important; however, in terms of data integrity, itis better to review the data flow diagram.
wrong_explanations.B: The lack of an adequate change control process can impact the integrity of the data; however, the system should be documented first to determine whether the transactions flow to other systems.
wrong_explanations.C: Evaluating the reconciliation controls helps to ensure data integrity; however, it is more important to understand the data flows of the application to ensure that the reconciliation controls are located in the correct place.

tips: Trap is A 'user access' — important but follows architectural understanding.
Trap is B 'change request process' — process review, comes after understanding flow.
Trap is C 'reconciliation controls' — placement depends on data flow understanding.
Data flow diagram first. Until the auditor understands HOW data moves between components, they can't evaluate WHERE controls should sit or whether they're effective.

questions.question: During the audit of an acquired software package, an information systems (IS) auditor finds that the software purchase was based on information obtained through the Internet, rather than from responses to a request for proposal. The IS auditor should FIRST:

options.A: test the software for compatibility with existing hardware.
options.D: ensure that the procedure had been approved.

questions.correct_explanation: In the case of a deviation from the predefined procedures, an IS auditor should first ensure that the procedure followed for acquiring the software is consistent with the business objectives and has been approved by the appropriate authorities.

wrong_explanations.A: Because the software package has already been acquired, it is most likely that it is in use and, therefore, compatible with existing hardware. Further, the first responsibility of the information systems (IS) auditor is to ensure that the purchasing procedures have been approved.
wrong_explanations.B: Because there was no request for proposal, there may be no documentation of the expectations of the product and nothing against which to measure a gap. The first task for the IS auditor is to ensure that the purchasing procedures were approved.
wrong_explanations.C: The licensing policy should be reviewed to ensure proper licensing but only after the purchasing procedures are checked.

tips: Trap is A 'compatibility testing' — late-cycle technical concern.
Trap is B 'gap analysis' — useful but premature without process verification.
Trap is C 'licensing review' — operational follow-up.
Acquisition deviating from procedures = procedure compliance issue first. Verify whether the deviation was authorized before evaluating the technical merits.

questions.question: A failure discovered in which of the following testing stages would have the GREATEST impact on the implementation of new application software?

options.D: Unit testing

questions.correct_explanation: Acceptance testing is the final stage before the software is installed and available for use. Software failure at the acceptance testing level has the greatest impact on implementation because this can result in delays and cost overruns.

wrong_explanations.A: System testing is undertaken by the development team to determine if the combined units of software work together and that the software meets user requirements per specifications. A failure here is expensive but easier to fix than a failure found later in the testing process.
wrong_explanations.C: Integration testing examines the units/modules as one integrated system. A failure here is expensive and requires re-work of the modules but is not as expensive as a problem found just prior to implementation.
wrong_explanations.D: Unit testing examines the individual units or components of the software. A failure here is expensive and requires re-work of the modules but is not as expensive as a problem found just prior to implementation. System, integration and unit testing are all performed by the developers at various stages of development; the impact of failure is comparatively less for each than failure at the acceptance testing stage.

tips: Trap is A 'system testing' — earlier stage; failures here can be fixed before deployment.
Trap is C 'integration testing' — earlier; modules can be reworked.
Trap is D 'unit testing' — earliest; cheapest to fix.
Acceptance testing is the LAST checkpoint before go-live. Failure here delays deployment and forces emergency rework, often disrupting business plans tied to the launch date.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST likely benefit of implementing a standardized infrastructure?

options.A: Improved cost-effectiveness of IT service delivery and operational support
options.B: Increased security of the IT service delivery center
options.C: Reduced level of investment in the IT infrastructure
options.D: Reduced need for testing future application changes

questions.correct_explanation: A standardized IT infrastructure provides a consistent set of platforms and operating systems across the organization. This standardization reduces the time and effort required to manage a set of disparate platforms and operating systems. In addition, the implementation of enhanced operational support tools (e.g., password management tools, patch management tools and auto provisioning of user access) is simplified. These tools can help the organization reduce the cost of IT service delivery and operational support.

wrong_explanations.B: A standardized infrastructure results in a more homogeneous environment, which is more prone to attacks.
wrong_explanations.C: While standardization can reduce support costs, the transition to a standardized kit can be expensive; therefore, the overall level of IT infrastructure investment is not likely to be reduced.
wrong_explanations.D: A standardized infrastructure may simplify testing of changes, but it does not reduce the need for such testing.

tips: Trap is B 'increased security' — possible but standardization isn't security-driven.
Trap is C 'reduced infrastructure investment' — opposite; standardization may require initial investment.
Trap is D 'no testing of future changes' — overstated; testing is still required.
Standardization reduces operational complexity: fewer platforms to support, common tooling, easier patching/monitoring. Cost-effectiveness is the most direct benefit.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST important factor in the design of a data warehouse?

options.D: Vulnerability of the system

questions.correct_explanation: Quality of the metadata is the most important element in the design of a data warehouse. A data warehouse is a copy of transaction data specifically structured for query and analysis. Metadata describes the data in the warehouse and aims to provide a table of contents to the stored information. Organizations that have built warehouses believe that metadata are the most important component of the warehouse.

wrong_explanations.B: A data warehouse is used for analysis and research, not for production operations, so the speed of transactions is not relevant.
wrong_explanations.C: Data in a data warehouse are frequently received from many sources and vast amounts of information may be received on an hourly or daily basis. Except to ensure adequate storage capability, this is not a primary concern of the designer.
wrong_explanations.D: Data warehouses may contain sensitive information or can be used to research sensitive information, so the security of the data warehouse is important. However, this is not the primary concern of the designer.

tips: Trap is B 'transaction speed' — important but warehouses prioritize query/analysis, not transaction speed.
Trap is C 'data volatility' — characteristic, not design driver.
Trap is D 'system vulnerability' — security concern, not design factor.
Metadata describes what's in the warehouse — without it, queries can't reliably interpret the data. Quality metadata is foundational for analytical use.

questions.question: Ideally, stress testing should be carried out in a:

options.D: production environment using test data.

questions.correct_explanation: Stress testing is carried out to ensure that a system can cope with production workloads. Testing with production-level workloads is important to ensure that the system will operate effectively when moved into production.

wrong_explanations.A: A test environment should always be used to avoid damaging the production environment, but testing only with test data may not test all aspects of the system adequately.
wrong_explanations.B: Testing should never take place in a production environment.
