wrong_explanations.D: It is not advisable to do stress testing in a production environment. Additionally, if only test data are used, there is no certainty that the system was stress tested adequately.

tips: Trap is A 'test environment with test data' — small-volume data won't reveal capacity issues.
Trap is B 'production environment with live workloads' — risk of breaking production.
Trap is D 'production with test data' — production environment good but test data won't stress it.
Stress testing's purpose: confirm system handles real production load. Use a test environment (safe) with production-realistic workloads (meaningful).

questions.question: Assignment of process ownership is essential in system development projects because it:

options.A: enables the tracking of the development completion percentage.
options.B: optimizes the design cost of user acceptance test cases.
options.C: minimizes the gaps between requirements and functionalities.
options.D: ensures that system design is based on business needs.

questions.correct_explanation: The involvement of process owners ensures that the system will be designed according to the needs of the business processes that depend on system functionality. A sign-off on the design by the process owners is crucial before development begins.

wrong_explanations.A: Process ownership assignment does not have a feature to track the completion percentage of deliverables.
wrong_explanations.B: Whether the design cost of test cases will be optimized is not determined from the assignment of process ownership. It may help to some extent; however, there are many other factors involved in the design of test cases.
wrong_explanations.C: For gap minimization, a specific requirements analysis framework should be in place and then applied; however, a gap may be found between the design and the as-built system that can lead to system functionality not meeting requirements. This will be identified during user acceptance testing. Process ownership alone does not have the capability to minimize requirement gaps.

tips: Trap is A 'tracking completion' — measurement, not design driver.
Trap is B 'optimize UAT cost' — secondary benefit.
Trap is C 'minimize requirements gap' — outcome of process owner involvement, not the reason for it.
Process owners know the business processes the system must support. Without them, design risks being technically correct but business-misaligned.

questions.question: The BEST time for an information systems (IS) auditor to assess the control specifications of a new application software package that is being considered for acquisition is during:

options.B: testing and prior to user acceptance.
options.D: the implementation phase.

questions.correct_explanation: The best time for the involvement of an IS auditor is at the beginning of the requirements definition of the development or acquisition of applications software, providing maximum opportunity for review of the vendors and their products. Early engagement of an IS auditor also minimizes the potential of a business commitment to a given solution that might be inadequate and more difficult to overcome as the process continues.

wrong_explanations.A: During testing, the information systems (IS) auditor ensures that the security requirements are met. This is not the time to assess the control specifications.
wrong_explanations.B: The control specifications drive the security requirements that are built into the contract and should be assessed before the product is acquired and tested.
wrong_explanations.D: During the implementation phase, the IS auditor may check whether the controls have been enabled; however, this is not the time to assess the control requirements.

tips: Trap is A 'lab testing phase' — too late; system is being tested.
Trap is B 'before user acceptance' — also too late; testing already happening.
Trap is D 'implementation phase' — far too late.
IS auditor reviewing control specifications during requirements gathering = maximum influence with minimum disruption. Earlier = cheaper to fix.

questions.question: The phases and deliverables of a system development life cycle project should be determined:

options.A: during the initial planning stages of the project.
options.B: after early planning has been completed but before work has begun.
options.C: throughout the work stages, based on risk and exposures.
options.D: only after all risk and exposures have been identified and the information systems (IS) auditor has recommended appropriate controls.

questions.correct_explanation: It is extremely important that the project is planned properly and that the specific phases and deliverables are identified during the early stages of the project. This enables project tracking and resource management.

wrong_explanations.B: Determining the deliverables and time lines of a project are a part of the early project planning work.
wrong_explanations.C: The requirements may change over the life of a project, but the initial deliverables should be documented from the beginning of the project.
wrong_explanations.D: Risk management is a never-ending process, so project planning cannot wait until all risk has been identified.

tips: Trap is B 'after early planning' — vague; planning IS where phases get defined.
Trap is C 'during work, based on risk' — emergent planning misses early phase definition.
Trap is D 'after risk identification + auditor recommendations' — too constrained; project planning shouldn't wait on auditors.
Phases and deliverables defined upfront enables tracking, resource allocation, and milestone management. Without early definition, projects drift without measurable progress.

questions.question: Management observed that the initial phase of a multiphase implementation was behind schedule and over budget. Prior to commencing with the next phase, an information systems (IS) auditor's PRIMARY suggestion for a postimplementation focus should be to:

options.A: assess whether the planned cost benefits are being measured, analyzed and reported.
options.B: review control balances and verify that the system is processing data accurately.
options.C: review the impact of program changes made during the first phase on the remainder of the project.
options.D: determine whether the system's objectives were achieved.

questions.correct_explanation: Because management is aware that the project had problems, reviewing the subsequent impact provides insight into the types and potential causes of the project issues. This insight helps to identify whether IT has adequately planned for those issues in subsequent projects.

wrong_explanations.A: While all choices are valid, the postimplementation focus and primary objective should be understanding the impact of the problems in the first phase on the remainder of the project.
wrong_explanations.B: The review should assess whether the control is working correctly but should focus on the problems that led to project overruns in budget and time.
wrong_explanations.D: Ensuring that the system works is a primary objective for the information systems (IS) auditor, but, in this case, because the project planning was a failure, the IS auditor should focus on the reasons for, and impact of, the failure.

tips: Trap is A 'cost benefits' — relevant but doesn't address WHY phase 1 went over.
Trap is B 'control balances' — operational verification, not the strategic learning.
Trap is D 'system objectives achieved' — success measurement, not learning.
Phase 1's problems likely affect phase 2+. Reviewing impact of those changes gives forward-looking insight — what to mitigate before next phase repeats the same mistakes.

questions.question: When implementing an application software package, which of the following presents the GREATEST risk?

options.B: Source programs that are not synchronized with object code
options.D: Programming errors

questions.correct_explanation: Parameters that are not set correctly is the greatest concern when implementing an application software package. Incorrectly set parameters are an immediate problem that can lead to system breach, failure or noncompliance.

wrong_explanations.A: Having multiple versions is a problem, but if the correct version is implemented, the most serious risk during implementation is to have the parameters for the program set incorrectly.
wrong_explanations.B: Lack of synchronization between source and object code is a serious risk for later maintenance of compiled programs but does not affect other types of programs and is not the most serious risk at the time of implementation.
wrong_explanations.D: Programming errors should be found during testing, not at the time of implementation.

tips: Trap is A 'multiple software versions' — version control issue, manageable.
Trap is B 'source/object code mismatch' — change control issue, eventually surfaces.
Trap is D 'programming errors' — software quality concern, present in all systems.
Incorrect parameters at go-live = immediate failure or vulnerability. Common with packages because parameters are often invisible until exercised in production.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of prototyping?

options.A: The finished system normally has strong internal controls.
options.B: Prototype systems can provide significant time and cost savings.
options.C: Change control is often less complicated with prototype systems.
options.D: Prototyping ensures that functions or extras are not added to the intended system.

questions.correct_explanation: Prototype systems can provide significant time and cost savings through better user interaction and the ability to rapidly adapt to changing requirements; however, they also have several disadvantages, including loss of overall security focus, project oversight and implementation of a prototype that is not yet ready for production.

wrong_explanations.A: Prototyping often has poor internal controls because the focus is primarily on functionality, not on security.
wrong_explanations.C: Change control becomes much more complicated with prototyping.
wrong_explanations.D: Prototyping often leads to functions or extras being added to the system that were not originally intended.

tips: Trap is A 'strong internal controls' — opposite; prototyping often UNDER-emphasizes controls.
Trap is C 'simpler change control' — opposite; change control is HARDER with prototyping.
Trap is D 'no extra functions' — opposite; prototyping invites scope creep.
Prototyping's actual benefit: rapid feedback loops with users → faster delivery, better fit, lower wrong-system risk. Quality and control are tradeoffs, not advantages.

questions.question: The PRIMARY objective of performing a post-incident review is that it presents an opportunity to:

options.B: harden the network to industry good practices.
options.C: highlight the importance of incident response management to management.
options.D: improve employee awareness of the incident response process.

questions.correct_explanation: A post-incident review examines the cause and response to an incident. The lessons learned from the review can be used to improve internal controls. Understanding the purpose and structure ofpost-incident reviews and follow-up procedures enables the information security manager to continuously improve the security program. Improving the incident response plan based on the incident review is an internal (corrective) control.

wrong_explanations.B: A post-incident review may result in improvements to controls, but its primary purpose is not to harden a network.
wrong_explanations.C: The purpose of post-incident review is to ensure that the opportunity is presented to learn lessons from the incident. It is not intended as a forum to educate management.
wrong_explanations.D: An incident may be used to emphasize the importance of incident response, but that is not the intention of the post-incident review.

tips: Trap is B 'harden the network' — operational outcome, narrow.
Trap is C 'highlight importance to management' — political objective, secondary.
Trap is D 'employee awareness' — training outcome, secondary.
Post-incident review's PRIMARY purpose: improve internal controls. Each incident teaches what controls failed; the review converts that into control improvements.

questions.question: An advantage of using sanitized live transactions for test data is that:

options.B: every error condition is likely to be tested.
options.C: no special routines are required to assess the results.
options.D: test transactions are representative of live processing.

questions.correct_explanation: Test data is representative of live processing; however, it is important that all sensitive information in the live transaction file is sanitized to prevent improper data disclosure.

wrong_explanations.A: Sanitized production data may not contain all transaction types. The test data may need to be modified to ensure that all data types are represented.
wrong_explanations.B: Not all error types are sure to be tested because most production data only contains certain types of errors.
wrong_explanations.C: The results can be tested using normal routines, but that is not a significant advantage of using sanitized live data.

tips: Trap is A 'all transaction types included' — depends on what live data was sanitized.
Trap is B 'every error condition tested' — live data won't necessarily exercise all errors.
Trap is C 'no special routines for results' — incorrect; results still need analysis.
Sanitized live data preserves real-world transaction patterns — frequencies, distributions, edge cases. More realistic than synthetic test data, safer than raw production.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor's PRIMARY concern when application developers wish to use a copy of yesterday's production transaction file for volume tests is that:

options.A: users may prefer to use contrived data for testing.
options.B: unauthorized access to sensitive data may result.
options.C: error handling and credibility checks may not be fully proven.
options.D: the full functionality of the new process may not necessarily be tested.

questions.correct_explanation: Unless the data are sanitized, there is a risk of disclosing sensitive data.

wrong_explanations.A: Production data are easier for users to use for comparison purposes.
wrong_explanations.C: There is a risk that former production data may not test all error routines; however, this is not as serious as the risk of release of sensitive data.
wrong_explanations.D: Using a copy of production data may not test all functionality, but this is not as serious as the risk of disclosure of sensitive data.

tips: Trap is A 'users prefer contrived data' — possible but not the audit concern.
Trap is C 'error handling not proven' — testing concern, not the primary audit concern.
Trap is D 'full functionality not tested' — coverage concern, secondary.
Production data in test environments without sanitization = sensitive data exposure to people who normally wouldn't have access. Privacy/regulatory risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is the PRIMARY purpose for conducting parallel testing?

options.A: To determine whether the system is cost-effective
options.B: To enable comprehensive unit and system testing
options.C: To highlight errors in the program interfaces with files
options.D: To ensure the new system meets user requirements

questions.correct_explanation: The purpose of parallel testing is to ensure that the implementation of a new system will meet user requirements by comparing the results of the old system with the new system to ensure correct processing.

wrong_explanations.A: Parallel testing may show that the old system is more cost-effective than the new system, but this is not the primary reason for parallel testing.
wrong_explanations.B: Unit and system testing are completed before parallel testing.
wrong_explanations.C: Program interfaces with files are tested for errors during system testing.

tips: Trap is A 'cost-effectiveness' — financial test, not parallel testing's purpose.
Trap is B 'unit and system testing' — earlier-stage tests, not parallel.
Trap is C 'program interface errors' — technical concern, addressable in unit/integration test.
Parallel testing runs old and new systems with the same data. Output comparison reveals whether the new system meets user requirements — by direct comparison to the known-good old system.

questions.question: The knowledge base of an expert system that uses questionnaires to lead the user through a series of choices before a conclusion is reached is known as:

options.D: dataflow diagrams.

questions.correct_explanation: Decision trees use questionnaires to lead a user through a series of choices until a conclusion is reached.

wrong_explanations.A: Rules refer to the expression of declarative knowledge using if-then relationships.
wrong_explanations.C: Semantic nets consist of a graph in which nodes represent physical or conceptual objects and the arcs describe the relationship between the nodes.
wrong_explanations.D: A dataflow diagram is used to map the progress of data through a system and examine logic, error handling and data management.

tips: Trap is A 'rules' — production rule systems, different structure.
Trap is C 'semantic nets' — graph-based knowledge representation, not questionnaire-based.
Trap is D 'dataflow diagrams' — process modeling tool, not knowledge representation.
Decision trees encode 'if X then Y else Z' branching as a tree. Questionnaires walking users through choices map directly to this structure.

questions.question: An advantage of using a bottom-up versus a top-down approach to software testing is that:

options.B: confidence in the system is achieved earlier.
options.C: errors in critical modules are detected earlier.
options.D: major functions and processing are tested earlier.

questions.correct_explanation: The bottom-up approach to software testing begins with the testing of atomic units, such as programs and modules, and works upward until complete system testing has taken place. The advantage of using a bottom-up approach to software testing is that errors in critical modules are found earlier.

wrong_explanations.A: Interface errors will not be found until later in the testing process-during integration or system testing.
wrong_explanations.B: Confidence in the system cannot be obtained until the testing is completed.
wrong_explanations.D: Bottom-up testing tests individual components and major functions and processing is not adequately tested until systems and integration testing is completed.

tips: Trap is A 'interface errors detected earlier' — that's TOP-DOWN's advantage.
Trap is B 'confidence achieved earlier' — top-down builds confidence in the architecture earlier.
Trap is D 'major functions tested earlier' — also top-down.
Bottom-up tests atomic units first — programs, modules. Critical-module errors surface immediately, before they cascade through the system. Defect cost lower when caught early at unit level.

questions.question: During which of the following phases in system development are user acceptance testing (UAT) plans normally prepared?

options.D: Postimplementation review

questions.correct_explanation: During requirements definition, the project team works with the users to define their precise objectives and functional needs. The users should be working with the team to consider and document how the system functionality can be tested to ensure that it meets their stated needs. An information systems {IS) auditor should know at what point user testing should be planned to ensure that it is most effective and efficient.

wrong_explanations.A: The feasibility study is too early for such detailed user involvement.
wrong_explanations.C: The implementation planning phase is when the tests are conducted. It is too late in the process to develop the test plan.
wrong_explanations.D: User acceptance testing (UAT) should be completed prior to implementation.

tips: Trap is A 'feasibility study' — too early; user requirements not yet defined.
Trap is C 'implementation planning' — too late; UAT plans should be ready by then.
Trap is D 'postimplementation review' — way too late; UAT happens before implementation.
Requirements definition is when users articulate what they need. UAT plans get authored alongside, asking 'how will we test that requirement?' Same time, same conversation.

questions.question: The use of object-oriented design and development techniques MOST likely:

options.A: facilitates the ability to reuse modules.
options.D: speeds up the system development life cycle (SDLC).

questions.correct_explanation: One of the major benefits of object-oriented design and development is the ability to reuse modules.

wrong_explanations.B: Object-oriented design is not intended as a method of improving system performance.
wrong_explanations.C: Control effectiveness is not an objective of object-oriented design; control effectiveness may be reduced through this approach.
wrong_explanations.D: The use of object-oriented design may speed up the system development life cycle (SDLC) for future projects through the reuse of modules, but object-oriented design does not speed up develfment of the initial project.

tips: Trap is B 'improves performance' — abstraction can ADD overhead, not improve performance.
Trap is C 'enhances control effectiveness' — control depends on design, not paradigm.
Trap is D 'speeds up SDLC' — initial OO design takes longer; speed comes later via reuse.
Object-oriented design's signature benefit: encapsulation enables modules to be reused across projects. That's where the long-term productivity gains come from.

questions.question: Which of the following should be included in a feasibility study for a project to implement an electronic data interchange (EDI) process?

options.D: Proposed trusted third-party agreement

questions.correct_explanation: The communications protocols must be included because there may be significant cost implications if new hardware and software are involved, and risk implications if the technology is new to the organization.

wrong_explanations.A: Encryption algorithms are too detailed for this phase. They would only be outlined, and any cost or performance implications would be shown.
wrong_explanations.B: Internal control procedures are too detailed for this phase. They would only be outlined, and any cost or performance implications would be shown.
wrong_explanations.D: Third-party agreements are too detailed for this phase. They would only be outlined, and any cost or performance implications would be shown.

tips: Trap is A 'encryption algorithm format' — implementation detail, downstream of feasibility.
Trap is B 'detailed internal control procedures' — also detailed; feasibility is high-level.
Trap is D 'trusted third-party agreement' — operational detail.
Communication protocols drive feasibility — they determine hardware/software requirements, costs, and integration complexity. Without protocol clarity, the feasibility study can't estimate.

questions.question: When a new system is to be implemented within a short time frame, it is MOST important to:

options.D: ensure that the code has been documented and reviewed.

questions.correct_explanation: It is most important to complete the user acceptance testing to ensure that the system to be implemented is working correctly.

wrong_explanations.A: The completion of the user manuals is less important than the need to test the system adequately.
wrong_explanations.C: Adding another enhancement increases the time to complete a project because the code must be frozen and testing must be completed, then any other changes as future enhancements must be made.
wrong_explanations.D: It is appropriate to have the code documented and reviewed, but, unless the acceptance testir,ig.is completed, there is no guarantee that the system will work correctly and meet user requirements.

tips: Trap is A 'finish writing user manuals' — documentation; can follow implementation.
Trap is C 'add last-minute enhancements' — exactly what to AVOID under time pressure.
Trap is D 'documented and reviewed code' — process discipline; secondary to functional verification.
UAT is the only test that confirms the system actually works for users. Skipping UAT under time pressure = high risk of go-live failure. Documentation can wait; functional validation can't.

questions.question: After an organization finishes the business process reengineering (BPR) of all its critical operations, an information systems (IS) auditor is MOST likely to focus on a review of:

options.D: continuous improvement and monitoring plans.

questions.correct_explanation: An IS auditor's task is to identify and ensure that key controls have been incorporated into the reengineered process.

wrong_explanations.A: An information systems (IS) auditor must review the process as it is today, not as it was in the past.
wrong_explanations.C: Business process reengineering (BPR) project plans are a step within a BPR project.
wrong_explanations.D: Continuous improvement and monitoring plans are steps within a BPR project.

tips: Trap is A 'pre-BPR flowcharts' — historical context, not the audit subject.
Trap is C 'BPR project plans' — process documentation, not control implementation.
Trap is D 'continuous improvement plans' — forward-looking, doesn't validate current controls.
Post-BPR flowcharts show the NEW process. Auditor checks that key controls were preserved or properly redesigned in the new process — the actual deliverable to validate.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor finds that a system under development has 12 linked modules and each item of data can carry up to IO definable attribute fields. The system handles several million transactions a year. Which of the following techniques can an IS auditor use to estimate the size of the development effort?

options.D: White box testing

questions.correct_explanation: Function point analysis is a technique used to determine the size of a development task based on the number of function points. Function points are factors such as inputs, outputs, inquiries and logical internal sites.

wrong_explanations.A: Program evaluation review technique (PERT) is a project management technique used in the planning and control of system projects.
wrong_explanations.C: The number of source lines of code gives a direct measure of program size, but it does not allow for the complexity that may be caused by multiple, linked modules and a variety of inputs and outputs.
wrong_explanations.D: White box testing involves a detailed review of the behavior of program code. It is a quality assurance technique suited to simpler applications during the design and building stage of development.

tips: Trap is A 'PERT' — estimates project DURATION, not size of effort.
Trap is C 'source lines of code' — old technique, doesn't scale to complex systems.
Trap is D 'white box testing' — testing technique, not estimation.
Function point analysis quantifies system size by counting inputs, outputs, queries, files, and interfaces. Specifically designed for development effort estimation.

questions.question: An organization has contracted with an external consulting firm to implement a commercial financial system to replace its existing system that was developed in-house. In reviewing the proposed development approach, which of the following is of GREATEST concern?

options.A: Acceptance testing is to be managed by users.
options.B: A quality plan is not part of the contracted deliverables.
options.C: Not all business functions will be available on initial implementation.
options.D: Prototyping is being used to confirm that the system meets business requirements.

questions.correct_explanation: A quality plan is an essential element of all projects. It is critical that the contracted supplier is required to produce such a plan. The quality plan for the proposed development contract should be comprehensive and encompass all phases of the development and include which business functions will be included and when.

wrong_explanations.A: Acceptance is normally managed by the user area because users must be satisfied that the new system will meet their requirements.
wrong_explanations.C: If the system is large, a phased-in approach to implementing the application is a reasonable approach.
wrong_explanations.D: Prototyping is a valid method of ensuring that the system will meet business requirements.

tips: Trap is A 'users manage acceptance testing' — appropriate; users own UAT.
Trap is C 'not all functions in initial release' — phased delivery is acceptable.
Trap is D 'prototyping for requirements confirmation' — valid technique.
Quality plan defines how the project ensures deliverables meet quality standards. Without it, quality is undefined and unmeasurable. Critical contractual deliverable.

questions.question: When preparing a business case to support the need of an electronic data warehouse solution, which of the following choices is the MOST important to assist management in the decision-making process?

options.D: Consult the audit department.

questions.correct_explanation: The business case should demonstrate feasibility for any potential project. By including a feasibility study in the business case along with a cost-benefit analysis, management can make an informed decision.

wrong_explanations.A: A business case should discuss all possible solutions to a given problem, which enables management to select the best option. This may include the option not to undertake the project.
wrong_explanations.B: It may be important to include security considerations in the business case if security is important to the solution and will address the problem; however, the feasibility study is more important and is necessary regardless of the type of problem.
wrong_explanations.D: Although the person preparing the business case may consult with the organization audit department, this is situational and not necessary to include in the business case.

tips: Trap is A 'discuss a single solution' — premature; alternatives should be considered.
Trap is B 'consider security controls' — important but a SUBSET of feasibility.
Trap is D 'consult audit department' — secondary input.
Feasibility study + cost-benefit demonstrates the proposal CAN work AND IS worth doing. That's what management needs to make an informed decision.

questions.question: Functionality is a characteristic associated with evaluating the quality of software products throughout their life cycle and is BEST described as the set of attributes that apply to the:

options.A: existence of a set of functions and their specified properties.
options.B: ability of the software to be transferred from one environment to another.
options.C: capability of software to maintain its level of performance under stated conditions.
options.D: relationship between the performance of the software and the amount of resources used.

questions.correct_explanation: Functionality is the set of attributes that apply to the existence of a set of functions and their specified properties. The functionality of a system represents the tasks, operations and purpose of the system in achieving its objective (i.e., supporting a business requirement).

wrong_explanations.B: The ability of the software to be transferred from one environment to another refers to portability.
wrong_explanations.C: The capability of software to maintain its level of performance under stated conditions refers to reliability.
wrong_explanations.D: The relationship between the performance of the software and the amount of resources used refers to efficiency.

tips: Trap is B 'transferred between environments' — that's PORTABILITY.
Trap is C 'maintain performance under stated conditions' — that's RELIABILITY.
Trap is D 'performance vs resources used' — that's EFFICIENCY.
Functionality = the FUNCTIONS the system performs and their specified properties. Other quality attributes describe how well functions perform; functionality is WHICH functions exist.

questions.question: During the development of an application, quality assurance (QA) testing and user acceptance testing (UAT) were combined. The MAJOR concern for an information systems (IS) auditor reviewing the project is:

options.D: delays in problem resolution.

questions.correct_explanation: The major risk of combining QA testing and UAT is that the users may apply pressure to accept a program that meets their needs even though it does not meet QA standards.

wrong_explanations.A: The method of testing used does not affect the maintenance of the system.
wrong_explanations.B: Quality assurance (QA)and user acceptance testing (UAT) are often led by business representatives according to a defined test plan. The combination of these two tests does not affect documentation.
wrong_explanations.D: The method of testing should not affect the timelines for problem resolution.

tips: Trap is A 'increased maintenance' — operational concern, not the immediate audit concern.
Trap is B 'improper testing documentation' — process concern, secondary.
Trap is D 'delays in problem resolution' — possible but not the primary risk.

QA tests against quality standards; UAT tests against user needs. Combined, users may pressure QA to accept programs that meet THEIR needs but fail QA standards. Independent QA pressure check is lost.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the role of an information systems (IS) auditor in improving quality assurance?

options.D: Consultant

questions.correct_explanation: Audit is primarily a quality control activity; however, the auditor can help an organization in improving quality assurance by guiding it on control effectiveness. This is the role of a consultant.

wrong_explanations.A: The internal auditor's role is to provide independent assurance that an organization's risk management, governance and internal control processes are operating effectively. This assurance is achieved by performing audits, which are quality control, and not necessarily related to quality assurance.
wrong_explanations.B: Review is primarily a quality control activity.
wrong_explanations.C: The information systems (IS) auditor may conduct workshops as a consultant in improving quality assurance, which is part of the planning activity.

tips: Trap is A 'internal auditor' — that's the role, not the QA improvement contribution.
Trap is B 'reviewer' — describes audit activity, not QA improvement role.
Trap is C 'workshop facilitator' — possible activity, not the broader role.
When helping improve QA (vs auditing it), the IS auditor consults — providing expertise and guidance without operating QA themselves. Maintains independence while adding value.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing a proposed application software acquisition should ensure that the:

options.A: operating system (OS) being used is compatible with the existing hardware platform.
options.B: planned OS updates have been scheduled to minimize negative impacts on enterprise needs.
options.C: OS has the latest versions and updates.
options.D: product is compatible with the current or planned OS.

questions.correct_explanation: In reviewing the proposed application, the auditor should ensure that the products to be purchased are compatible with the current or planned OS.

wrong_explanations.A: If the operating system (OS) is currently being used, it is compatible with the existing hardware platform; if it were incompatible, it would not operate properly.
wrong_explanations.B: The planned OS updates should be scheduled to minimize negative impacts on the organization, but this is not an issue when considering the acquisition of new software.
wrong_explanations.C: The installed OS should be equipped with the most recent versions and updates (with sufficient history and stability). Because the OS is installed, it is not a consideration at the time of considering acquisition of a new application.

tips: Trap is A 'OS compatible with hardware' — that's a hardware/OS relationship, not application-OS.
Trap is B 'OS update schedule' — operations concern, not acquisition fit.
Trap is C 'OS has latest versions' — patching concern, not application compatibility.
Application acquisition's OS concern: does the application work with the OS we have or are about to have? Past or future OS plans matter; the version cadence doesn't.

questions.question: Which of the following is of GREATEST concern to an information systems (IS) auditor when performing an audit of a client relationship management system migration project?

options.A: The technical migration is planned for a Friday preceding a long weekend, and the time window is too short for completing all tasks.
options.B: Employees pilot testing the system are concerned that the data representation in the new system is completely different from the old system.
options.C: A single implementation is planned, immediately decommissioning the legacy system.
options.D: Five weeks prior to the target date, there are still numerous defects in the printing functionality of the new system's software.

questions.correct_explanation: Major system migrations should include a phase of parallel operation or a phased cutover to reduce implementation risk. Decommissioning or disposing of the old hardware would complicate any fallback strategy if the new system does not operate correctly.

wrong_explanations.A: A weekend can be used as a time buffer so that the new system will have a better chance of being up and running after the weekend.
wrong_explanations.B: A different data representation does not mean different data presentation at the front end. Even when this is the case, this issue can be solved by adequate training and user support.
wrong_explanations.D: The printing functionality is commonly one of the last functions to be tested in a new system because it is usually the last step performed in any business event. Thus, meaningful testing and the respective error fixing are only possible after all other parts of the software have been successfully tested.

tips: Trap is A 'long weekend Friday cutover' — common practice; tight window manageable.
Trap is B 'data representation different' — UX concern, addressable through training.
Trap is D 'printing defects 5 weeks out' — concerning but recoverable before launch.
Direct cutover with legacy decommissioning = no fallback path. If the new system fails, operations halt. Migration projects need parallel operation or phased cutover for safety.

questions.question: Which of the following types of testing determines whether a new or modified system can operate in its target environment without adversely impacting other existing systems?

options.D: Sociability testing

questions.correct_explanation: The purpose of sociability testing is to confirm that a new or modified system can operate in its target environment without adversely impacting existing systems. This should cover the platform that will perform primary application processing and interfaces with other systems, and changes to the desktop in a client-server or web development.

wrong_explanations.A: Parallel testing is the process of feeding data into two systems-the modified system and an alternate system-and comparing the results. In this approach, the old and new systems operate concurrently for a period and perform the same processing functions. This allows a new system to be tested without affecting existing systems.
wrong_explanations.B: Pilot testing takes place first at one location and is then extended to other locations. The purpose is to see if the new system operates satisfactorily in one place before implementing it at other locations. In most cases, the cutover to the new system will disable existing systems.
wrong_explanations.C: Interface/integration testing is a hardware or software test that evaluates the connection of two or more components that pass information from one area to another. The objective is to take unit-tested modules and build an integrated structure. This does not test in a true production environment.

tips: Trap is A 'parallel testing' — runs old + new with same data, doesn't test environmental impact.
Trap is B 'pilot testing' — limited rollout, doesn't test environmental compatibility comprehensively.
Trap is C 'interface/integration testing' — tests between components within the system.
Sociability testing answers: does this system COEXIST peacefully with the other systems in production? Tests interactions with the broader environment, not internal components.

questions.question: At the end of the testing phase of software development, an information systems (IS) auditor observes that an intermittent software error has not been corrected. No action has been taken to resolve the error. The IS auditor should:

options.A: report the error as a finding and leave further exploration to the auditee's discretion.
options.C: recommend that problem resolution be escalated.
options.D: ignore the error because it is not possible to get objective evidence for the software error.

questions.correct_explanation: When an IS auditor observes such conditions, it is best to fully apprise the auditee and suggest that further problem resolutions be attempted, including escalation if necessary.

wrong_explanations.A: Recording it as a minor error and leaving it to the auditee's discretion is inappropriate. Action should be taken before the application goes into production.
wrong_explanations.B: The information systems (IS) auditor is not authorized to resolve the error.
wrong_explanations.D: Neglecting the error indicates that the IS auditor has not taken steps to further probe the issue to its logical end.

tips: Trap is A 'report and leave to auditee' — passive; auditor should advocate for resolution.
Trap is B 'attempt to resolve' — auditor doesn't fix; that's a SoD violation.
Trap is D 'ignore lacks evidence' — defeatist; intermittent doesn't mean unverifiable.
When auditor sees an unresolved error at testing-phase end, the response is to ESCALATE — push for resolution before the system goes live. Reporting alone doesn't drive action.

questions.question: Which of the following is the GREATEST risk to the effectiveness of application system controls?

options.D: Unresolved regulatory compliance issues

questions.correct_explanation: Collusion is an active attack where users collaborate to bypass controls, such as separation ofduties. Such breaches may be difficult to identify because even well-thought-out application controls may be circumvented.

wrong_explanations.A: Automation should remove manual processing steps wherever possible. The only risk is the removal of manual security controls without replacement with automated controls.
wrong_explanations.B: The lack of documentation is a problem on many systems but not a serious risk in most cases.
wrong_explanations.D: Unregulated compliance issues are a risk but do not measure the effectiveness of the controls.

tips: Trap is A 'removal of manual steps' — automation reduces some risks (errors), increases others.
Trap is B 'inadequate procedure manuals' — control weakness, addressable through documentation.
Trap is D 'unresolved compliance issues' — important but specific, not the GREATEST risk to controls effectiveness.
Collusion between employees defeats SoD-based controls. When colluding parties cooperate to bypass checks, even well-designed controls fail. Hardest to detect.

questions.question: An organization is implementing a new system to replace a legacy system. Which of the following conversion practices creates the GREATEST risk?

options.D: Phased

questions.correct_explanation: Direct cutover implies switching to the new system immediately, usually without the ability to revert to the old system in the event of problems. This approach has the highest risk and may have a significant impact on the organization.

wrong_explanations.A: A pilot implementation is the implementation of the system at a single location or region and then a rollout of the system to the rest of the organization, after the application and implementation plan have been proven to work correctly at the pilot location.
wrong_explanations.B: A parallel test requires running the old and new systems in parallel for a time period. This test highlights any problems or inconsistencies between the old and new systems.
wrong_explanations.D: A phased approach is used to implement the system in phases or sections-this minimizes the overall risk by only affecting one area at a time.

tips: Trap is A 'pilot' — limited rollout, low-risk testing approach.
Trap is B 'parallel' — safest; runs both systems together.
Trap is D 'phased' — graduated rollout, manageable risk.
Direct cutover = immediate switch with no rollback path. If the new system fails, operations halt. Highest-risk conversion strategy by far.

questions.question: During the requirements definition stage of a proposed enterprise resource planning system, the project sponsor requests that the procurement and accounts payable modules be linked. Which of the following test methods is the BEST to perform?

options.D: Quality assurance (QA) testing

questions.correct_explanation: Integration testing is a hardware or software test that evaluates the connection of two or more components that pass information from one area to another. The objective is to take unit-tested modules and build an integrated structure dictated by design.

wrong_explanations.A: Unit testing is a technique that is used to test program logic within a particular program or module and does not specifically address the linkage between software modules. Integration testing is the best answer.
wrong_explanations.C: Sociability testing confirms that the new or modified system can operate in its target environment without adversely impacting existing systems and does not specifically address the linkage between software modules. Integration testing is the best answer.
wrong_explanations.D: Quality assurance (QA) testing is primarily used to ensure that the logic of the application is correct and does not specifically address the linkage between software modules. Integration testing is the best answer.

tips: Trap is A 'unit testing' — individual modules; doesn't test inter-module connections.
Trap is C 'sociability testing' — tests interactions with EXTERNAL systems, not internal modules.
Trap is D 'QA testing' — quality assurance approach, not specific to inter-module connections.
Two modules being LINKED requires integration testing — verifying the connection passes data correctly between them. That's integration testing's specific job.

questions.question: During a postimplementation review of an enterprise resource management system, an information systems (IS) auditor is MOST likely to:

options.D: evaluate system testing.

questions.correct_explanation: Reviewing access control configuration is the first task performed to determine whether security has been appropriately mapped in the system.

wrong_explanations.B: Because a postimplementation review is done after user acceptance testing and actual implementation, an information systems (IS) auditor does not evaluate interface testing. Evaluating interface testing is part of the implementation process.
wrong_explanations.C: The issue of reviewing detailed design documentation is not generally relevant to an enterprise resource management system, because these systems are usually vendor packages with user manuals. Further, because the system has been implemented, the IS auditor would only check the detailed design if there appeared to be a gap between design and functionality.
wrong_explanations.D: System testing should be performed before final user signoff. The IS auditor should not need to review the system tests after implementation.

tips: Trap is B 'evaluate interface testing' — testing already happened pre-implementation.
Trap is C 'review detailed design documentation' — design phase artifact, less relevant post-implementation.
Trap is D 'evaluate system testing' — also pre-implementation activity.
Postimplementation review focuses on PRODUCTION configuration — particularly access controls, which determine ongoing security. First check: was security mapped correctly?

questions.question: An organization recently deployed a customer relationship management application that was developed in-house. Which of the following is the BEST option to ensure that the application operates as designed?

options.D: Management approval of the system

questions.correct_explanation: The purpose of a postimplementation review is to evaluate how successfully the project results match original goals, objectives and deliverables. The postimplementation review also evaluates how effective the project management practices were in keeping the project on track.

wrong_explanations.A: user acceptance testing (UAT) verifies that the system functionality is deemed acceptable by the end users of the system; however, a review of UAT does not validate whether the system is performing as designed because UAT is performed on a subset of system functionality. The UAT review is a part of the postimplementation review.
wrong_explanations.B: Although a risk assessment highlights the risk of the system, it does not include an analysis to verify that the system is operating as designed.
wrong_explanations.D: Management approval of the system can be based on reduced functionality and does not verify that the system is operating as designed. Management approval is a part of postimplementation review.

tips: Trap is A 'UAT' — pre-deployment validation; doesn't confirm production operation.
Trap is B 'project risk assessment' — planning phase activity, not operational confirmation.
Trap is D 'management approval' — administrative, doesn't validate operation.
Postimplementation review evaluates whether deployed system operates as designed AND delivers expected value. Specifically designed for this question.

questions.question: In an online transaction processing system, data integrity is maintained by ensuring that a transaction is either completed in its entirety or not at all. This principle of data integrity is known as:

options.D: durability.

questions.correct_explanation: The principle of atomicity requires that a transaction be completed in its entirety or not at all. If an error or interruption occurs, all changes made up to that point are backed out.

wrong_explanations.A: Isolation ensures that each transaction is isolated from other transactions; hence, each transaction can only access data if they are not being simultaneously accessed or modified by another process.
wrong_explanations.B: Consistency ensures that all integrity conditions in the database are maintained with each transaction.
wrong_explanations.D: Durability ensures that, when a transaction has been reported back to a user as complete, the resultant changes to the database will survive subsequent hardware or software failures.

tips: Trap is A 'isolation' — concurrent transactions don't interfere with each other.
Trap is B 'consistency' — database remains in valid state across transactions.
Trap is D 'durability' — committed transactions survive system failure.
Atomicity = all-or-nothing. Either every step of the transaction completes, or none of them do. Partial completion is impossible.

questions.question: An organization undertakes a business process reengineering project in support of a new and direct marketing approach to its customers. Which of the following is an information systems (IS) auditor's main concern about the new process?

options.A: Whether key controls are in place to protect assets and information resources
options.B: Whether the system addresses corporate customer requirements
options.C: Whether the system can meet the performance goals
options.D: Whether the system supports segregation/separation of duties (SoD)

questions.correct_explanation: The audit team must advocate the inclusion of the key controls and verify that the controls are in place before implementing the new process.

wrong_explanations.B: The system must meet the requirements of all customers, not just corporate customers. This is not the information systems (IS) auditor's main concern.
wrong_explanations.C: The system must meet performance requirements, but this is of secondary concern to the need to ensure that key controls are in place.
wrong_explanations.D: Separation of duties (SoD) is a key control-but only one of the controls that should be in place to protect the assets of the organization.

tips: Trap is B 'addresses customer requirements' — important but not the audit focus.
Trap is C 'meets performance goals' — operational concern, secondary.
Trap is D 'supports SoD' — one type of control, broader controls matter.
BPR can streamline processes but easily strips out controls in the name of efficiency. Auditor's PRIMARY concern: have the key controls been preserved or properly redesigned in the new process?

questions.question: An organization implemented a new client-server enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. Local branches transmit customer orders to a central manufacturing facility. Which of the following BEST ensures that the orders are processed accurately and the corresponding products are produced?

options.B: Logging all customer orders in the ERP system
options.C: Using hash totals in the order transmitting process
options.D: Approving (production supervisor) orders prior to production

questions.correct_explanation: Verification of the products produced ensures that the produced products match the orders in the order system.

wrong_explanations.B: Logging can be used to detect inaccuracies but does not guarantee accurate processing.
wrong_explanations.C: Hash totals ensure accurate order transmission but not accurate processing centrally.
wrong_explanations.D: Production supervisory approval is a time-consuming manual process that does not guarantee proper control.

tips: Trap is B 'logging customer orders' — record-keeping, doesn't ensure correct production.
Trap is C 'hash totals in transmission' — verifies transmission accuracy, not production accuracy.
Trap is D 'production supervisor approves' — preventive control, but doesn't verify post-production accuracy.
End-to-end verification: produced products match orders. Direct comparison from order entry to production output. Catches errors anywhere in the chain.

questions.question: When two or more systems are integrated, the information systems (IS) auditor must review input/output controls in the:

options.A: systems receiving the output of other systems.
options.B: systems sending output to other systems.
options.D: interfaces between the two systems.

questions.correct_explanation: Both systems must be reviewed for input/output controls because the output for one system is the input for the other.

wrong_explanations.A: A responsible control is to protect downstream systems from contamination from an upstream system. This requires a system that sends data to review its output and the receiving system to review its input.
wrong_explanations.B: Systems sending data to other systems should ensure that the data they send are correct, but that verification does not protect the receiving system from transmission errors.
wrong_explanations.D: The interfaces must be set up correctly and provide error controls, but a good practice is to review the data before sending and after receipt.

tips: Trap is A 'systems receiving output only' — half the picture.
Trap is B 'systems sending output only' — also half.
Trap is D 'interfaces only' — too narrow; output controls in the source system matter too.

When two systems integrate, output of one becomes input of another. Both ends need controls — sending side validates output quality; receiving side validates input. Controls must exist on BOTH systems.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor recommends that an initial validation control be programmed into a credit card transaction capture application. The initial validation process MOST likely:

options.A: checks to ensure that the type of transaction is valid for the card type.
options.B: verifies the format of the number entered, then locates it on the database.
options.C: ensures that the transaction entered is within the cardholder's credit limit.
options.D: confirms that the card is not shown as lost or stolen on the master file.

questions.correct_explanation: The initial validation should confirm whether the card is valid. This validity is established through the card number and personal identification number entered by the user.

wrong_explanations.A: The initial validation is not used to check the transaction type-just the validity of the card number.
wrong_explanations.C: The initial validation is to prove the card number entered is valid-only then can the transaction amount be checked for approval from the bank.
wrong_explanations.D: The verification that the card has not been reported as lost or stolen is only done after the card number has been validated as correctly entered.

tips: Trap is A 'transaction valid for card type' — business rule check, after card validation.
Trap is C 'within credit limit' — financial check, after card validation.
Trap is D 'not lost or stolen' — fraud check, after card identification.
Initial validation = does this card EXIST? Format check + database lookup. Without confirming the card itself is valid, downstream checks (limit, type, fraud) are meaningless.

questions.question: A small company cannot segregate duties between its development processes and its change control function. What is the BEST way to ensure that the tested code is the code that is moved into production?

options.D: Management approval of changes

questions.correct_explanation: Automated release management software can prevent unauthorized changes by moving code into production without any manual intervention.

wrong_explanations.B: Manual code comparison can detect whether the wrong code has been moved into production; however, code comparison does not prevent the code from being migrated and is not as good a control as using release management software. In addition, manual code comparison is not always efficient and requires highly skilled personnel.
wrong_explanations.C: Regression testing ensures that changes do not break the current system functionality or unwittingly overwrite previous changes. Regression testing does not prevent untested code from moving into production.
wrong_explanations.D: Although management should approve every change to production, approvals do not prevent untested code from being migrated into the production environment.

tips: Trap is B 'manual code comparison' — slow, error-prone, not scalable.
Trap is C 'regression testing in preproduction' — verifies functionality, doesn't enforce code identity.
Trap is D 'management approval' — administrative; doesn't prevent unauthorized code from being moved.
Release management software automates the move from test to production with no manual intervention. Tested code = released code, by tool design. Compensating control for SoD failure.

questions.question: Which of the following will BEST ensure the successful offshore development of business applications?

options.C: Awareness of cultural and political differences
options.D: Postimplementation review

questions.correct_explanation: When dealing with offshore operations, it is essential to create detailed specifications. Language differences, a lack of interaction between developers and physically remote end users can create gaps in communication in which assumptions and modifications may not be adequately communicated. Inaccurate specifications cannot easily be corrected.

wrong_explanations.A: Contract management practices, although important, do not ensure successful development if the specifications are incorrect.
wrong_explanations.C: Cultural and political differences, although important, should not affect the delivery of a good product.
wrong_explanations.D: Postimplementation review, although important, is too late in the process to ensure successful project delivery and is not as pivotal to the success of the project.

tips: Trap is A 'stringent contract management' — process discipline, doesn't prevent specification gaps.
Trap is C 'cultural and political awareness' — important but operational, not technical-success driver.
Trap is D 'postimplementation review' — too late; review can't fix offshore-development gaps.
Offshore = remote, less interactive. Detailed specifications fill the gap that proximity normally provides. Without them, assumptions diverge and the deliverable misses requirements.

questions.question: When planning to add personnel to tasks imposing time constraints on the duration of a project, which of the following should be revalidated FIRST?

options.D: Personnel assigned to other tasks

questions.correct_explanation: Adding resources may change the route of the critical path. The critical path must be reevaluated to ensure that additional resources will shorten the project duration.

wrong_explanations.A: Given that there may be slack time available on some of the other tasks that are not on the critical path, the resource allocation should be based on the project segments that affect delivery dates.
wrong_explanations.C: Given that there may be slack time available on some of the other tasks that are not on the critical path, a factor such as the length of other tasks may or may not be affected.
wrong_explanations.D: Depending on the skill level of the resources required or available, the addition of resources may not shorten the timeline. Therefore, the first step is to examine what resources are required to address the times on the critical path.

tips: Trap is A 'project budget' — important but doesn't determine whether more people shorten duration.
Trap is C 'remaining task length' — affected BY adding people, not the analysis target.
Trap is D 'personnel on other tasks' — operational concern.
Adding people to a project may NOT shorten duration if they aren't on the critical path. Brooks' Law: 'adding manpower to a late project makes it later'. Critical path drives the answer.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST helps organizations in optimizing audit resources and improving the quality of audits?

options.D: Risk-based audit approach

questions.correct_explanation: An integrated audit approach focuses on combining different types of audits at the same time; the results of different audit scopes can be shared to provide a focused and quality audit report.

wrong_explanations.A: An independent review of the audit helps in improving the quality of future audits but may not help in optimizing resources.
wrong_explanations.C: Global auditing standards help in improving the quality of an audit but may not help in optimizing resources.
wrong_explanations.D: A risk-based audit approach focuses on allocating resources to high-risk areas to make audits more effective but may not optimize resources.

tips: Trap is A 'independent review of audit work' — quality assurance, doesn't optimize resources.
Trap is C 'global auditing standards' — guidelines for HOW to audit, not optimization.
Trap is D 'risk-based audit approach' — focusing tactic, not multi-audit optimization.

Integrated audit combines multiple audit types into one engagement — financial + IS + operational + compliance. Shared scope, shared work, shared findings. Significant resource savings AND quality improvements.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of time box management?

options.A: Not suitable for prototyping or rapid application development
options.B: Eliminates the need for a quality process
options.C: Prevents cost overruns and delivery delays
options.D: Separates system and user acceptance testing (UAT)

questions.correct_explanation: Timebox management, by its nature, sets specific time and cost boundaries. It is effective in controlling costs and delivery timelines by ensuring that each segment of the project is divided into small controllable time frames.

wrong_explanations.A: Timebox management is very suitable for prototyping and rapid application development.
wrong_explanations.B: Timebox management does not eliminate the need for a quality process.
wrong_explanations.D: Timebox management integrates system and user acceptance testing (UAT).

tips: Trap is A 'not suitable for prototyping/RAD' — false; time boxing is COMMON in prototyping/RAD.
Trap is B 'eliminates quality process' — false; quality process is preserved within time boxes.
Trap is D 'separates system and UAT' — false; time boxing doesn't separate test types.
Time box management: fixed time, fixed cost, variable scope. Within each time box, the team delivers what fits. Strong cost/time control by design.

questions.question: The waterfall life cycle model of software development is MOST appropriately used when:

options.A: requirements are well understood and are expected to remain stable, like the business environment in which the system will operate.
options.B: requirements are well understood and the project is subject to time pressures.
options.C: the project intends to apply an object-oriented design and programming approach.
options.D: the project will involve the use of new technology.

questions.correct_explanation: Historically, the waterfall model has been best suited to stable conditions and well-defined requirements.

wrong_explanations.B: When the degree of uncertainty of the system to be delivered and the conditions in which it will be used rises, the waterfall model has not been successful. In these circumstances, the various forms of iterative development life cycle give the advantage of breaking down the scope of the overall system to be delivered, making the requirements gathering and design activities more manageable. The ability of an iterative development life cycle to deliver working software earlier also acts to alleviate uncertainty and may allow an earlier realization of benefits.
wrong_explanations.C: The choice of a design and programming approach is not, itself, a determining factor of the type of software development life cycle that is appropriate.
wrong_explanations.D: The use of new technology in a project introduces a significant element of risk. An iterative form of development, particularly one of the agile or exploratory methods that focuses on early development of actual working software, is likely to be the better option to manage this uncertainty.

tips: Trap is B 'time pressures' — agile or RAD better suit time pressure.
Trap is C 'object-oriented approach' — paradigm-independent; waterfall doesn't require/exclude OO.
Trap is D 'new technology' — waterfall is poor for new technology because requirements often change.
Waterfall = stable requirements, predictable environment, sequential phases. Best when you KNOW what you need upfront and the environment won't shift.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST critical when creating data for testing the logic in a new or modified application system?

options.A: Enough data for each test case
options.B: Data representing expected conditions in actual processing
options.D: A random sample of actual data

questions.correct_explanation: Selecting the right kind of data is key in testing a computer system. The data should not only include valid and invalid data but also be representative of actual processing; quality is more important than quantity.

wrong_explanations.A: The quantity of data for each test case is not as important as having test cases that address all types of operating conditions.
wrong_explanations.C: It is more important to have adequate test data than to complete the testing on schedule.
wrong_explanations.D: It is unlikely that a random sample of actual data covers all test conditions and provides a reasonable representation of actual data.

tips: Trap is A 'enough data per test case' — quantity, not quality.
Trap is C 'completing on schedule' — time concern, not data concern.
Trap is D 'random sample of actual data' — random may miss critical edge cases.
Test data must REPRESENT actual processing — valid data, invalid data, edge cases, error conditions. Realistic distribution of conditions matters more than volume or randomness.

questions.question: Which of the following should an information systems (IS) auditor review to gain an understanding of the effectiveness of controls over the management of multiple projects?

options.D: Program organization

questions.correct_explanation: Project portfolio information is the basis for project portfolio management. It includes project data, such as owner, schedules, objectives, project type, status and cost. Project portfolio management requires specific project portfolio reports.

wrong_explanations.A: Project information may contain the information about control effectiveness for one specific project and updates to various parameters pertaining to the current status of that single project.
wrong_explanations.B: Policy documents on project management set direction for the design, development, implementation and monitoring of the project.
wrong_explanations.D: Program organization is the team required (steering committee, quality assurance, systems personnel, analyst, programmer, hardware support, etc.) to meet the delivery objectives of the projects.

tips: Trap is A 'project information' — single-project view, doesn't show controls across multiple projects.
Trap is B 'policy documents' — define rules but don't show actual project status.
Trap is D 'program organization' — describes structure, not control effectiveness.
Multi-project oversight requires PORTFOLIO information — owners, schedules, statuses, costs across all projects. That's where multi-project controls become observable.

questions.question: Documentation of a business case used in an IT development project should be retained until:

options.A: the end of the system's life cycle.
options.D: the system is in production.

questions.correct_explanation: A business case should be used throughout the life cycle of the product. It serves as an anchor for new management personnel, helps to maintain focus and provides valuable information on estimates versus actuals. Questions, such as "Why do we do that?", "What was the original intent?" and "How did we perform against the plan?", can be answered, and lessons for developing future business cases can be learned.

wrong_explanations.B: The business case should be retained even after project approval to provide ability to review and validate the business case once the project is implemented.
wrong_explanations.C: The business case will be retained throughout the system development life cycle for later reference and validation.
wrong_explanations.D: After the system is in production, the business case can be validated to ensure that the promised costs and benefits were correct.

tips: Trap is B 'until project approved' — too short; business case is referenced throughout development.
Trap is C 'until user acceptance' — also too short.
Trap is D 'until production' — still too short.
Business case is a reference document for the SYSTEM'S ENTIRE LIFECYCLE — informing maintenance decisions, retirement decisions, new investment comparisons. Outlives the project.

questions.question: During the review of a web-based software development project, an information systems (IS) auditor realizes that coding standards are not enforced and code reviews are rarely carried out. These issues will MOST likely increase the likelihood of a successful:

options.D: war dialing attack.

questions.correct_explanation: Poorly written code, especially in web-based applications, is often exploited by hackers using buffer overflow techniques.

wrong_explanations.B: A brute force attack is used to crack passwords, but this is not related to coding standards.
wrong_explanations.C: A distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack floods its target with numerous packets to prevent it from responding to legitimate requests. This is not related to coding standards.
wrong_explanations.D: War dialing uses modem-scanning tools to hack private branch exchanges or other telecommunications services.

tips: Trap is B 'brute force attack' — targets passwords, unrelated to coding standards.
Trap is C 'DDoS attack' — network attack, unrelated to code quality.
Trap is D 'war dialing attack' — modem-era reconnaissance, irrelevant.
Buffer overflow exploits poorly-written code that doesn't validate input lengths. Web apps without coding standards or code reviews are particularly vulnerable to buffer overflows.

questions.question: Which testing approach is MOST appropriate to ensure that internal application interface errors are identified as soon as possible?

options.D: System testing

questions.correct_explanation: The top-down approach to testing ensures that interface errors are detected early and that testing of major functions is conducted early.

wrong_explanations.A: A bottom-up approach to testing begins with atomic units, such as programs and modules, and works upward until a complete system test has taken place.
wrong_explanations.B: Sociability testing takes place at a later stage in the development process.
wrong_explanations.D: System tests take place at a later stage in the development process.

tips: Trap is A 'bottom-up testing' — tests modules first, interfaces last; opposite of question's requirement.
Trap is B 'sociability testing' — tests external systems, not internal interfaces.
Trap is D 'system testing' — overall functionality test, not interface-focused.
Top-down testing exercises high-level functions first, then drills into modules. Interface errors surface immediately because interfaces are tested before underlying modules.

questions.question: When reviewing input controls, an information systems (IS) auditor observes that, in accordance with corporate policy, procedures allow supervisory override of data validation edits. The IS auditor should:

options.A: not be concerned, because there may be other compensating controls to mitigate the risk.
options.B: ensure that overrides are automatically logged and subject to review.
options.C: verify whether all such overrides are referred to senior management for approval.
options.D: recommend that overrides not be permitted.

questions.correct_explanation: If input procedures allow overrides of data validation and editing, automatic logging should occur. A management individual who did not initiate the override should review this log.

wrong_explanations.A: An information systems (IS) auditor should not assume that compensating controls exist.
wrong_explanations.C: The log may be reviewed by another manager but does not require senior management approval.
wrong_explanations.D: If the overrides are policy-compliant, there is no need for senior management approval or a blanket prohibition.

tips: Trap is A 'not concerned, compensating controls exist' — assumes; auditor must verify, not assume.
Trap is C 'overrides referred to senior management' — over-engineering; supervisory review is sufficient.
Trap is D 'recommend overrides not be permitted' — overrides are policy-allowed; auditor doesn't unilaterally restrict policy.
If overrides are policy-allowed, they need OPERATIONAL CONTROL: automatic logging + independent review. That's how the override capability stays governed.

questions.question: To minimize the cost of a software project, quality management techniques should be applied:

options.A: as close to their writing (i.e., point of origination) as possible.
options.B: primarily at project start to ensure that the project is established in accordance with organizational governance standards.
options.C: continuously throughout the project with an emphasis on finding and fixing defects primarily through testing to maximize the defect detection rate.
options.D: mainly at project close-down to capture lessons learned that can be applied to future projects.

questions.correct_explanation: Although quality management is important to properly establish a software development project, quality management should be effectively practiced throughout the project. The major source of unexpected costs on most software projects is rework. The general rule is that the earlier in the development life cycle that a defect occurs, and the longer it takes to find and fix that defect, the more effort will be needed to correct it. A well-written quality management plan is a good start, but it must also be actively applied. Simply relying on testing to identify defects is a relatively costly and less effective way of achieving software quality. For example, an error in requirements discovered in the testing phase can result in scrapping significant amounts of work.

wrong_explanations.A: Quality assurance (QA) should start as early as possible but continue through the entire development process.
wrong_explanations.B: Only performing QA during the start of the project will not detect problems that appear later in the development cycle.
wrong_explanations.D: Capturing lessons learned will be too late for the current project. Additionally, applying quality management techniques throughout a project is likely to yield its own insights into the causes of quality problems and assist in staff development.

tips: Trap is A 'as close to writing' — close, but the principle is broader.
Trap is B 'primarily at project start' — too narrow; project-start governance isn't enough.
Trap is D 'mainly at project close-down' — way too late; lessons-learned can't fix THIS project.

Continuous quality management with testing-driven defect detection minimizes total project cost. The earlier defects are found, the cheaper to fix; testing throughout (not just at end) keeps defect cost low.

questions.question: When identifying an earlier project completion time, which is to be accomplished by paying a premium for early completion, the activities that should be selected are those:

options.A: whose sum of activity time is the shortest.
options.C: that give the longest possible completion time.
options.D: whose sum of slack time is the shortest.

questions.correct_explanation: A critical path's activity time is longer than that for any other path through the network. This path is important because ifeverything goes as scheduled, its length gives the shortest possible completion time for the overall project. Activities on the critical path become candidates for crashing (i.e., for reduction in their time by payment of a premium for early completion). Activities on the critical path have zero slack time and, conversely, activities with zero slack time are on a critical path. By successively relaxing activities on a critical path, a curve showing total project costs versus time can be obtained.

wrong_explanations.A: Attention should focus on the tasks within the critical path that have no slack time.
wrong_explanations.C: The critical path is the longest time length of the activities but is not based on the longest time of any individual activity.
wrong_explanations.D: A task on the critical path has no slack time.

tips: Trap is A 'shortest activity time' — irrelevant; time on critical path matters.
Trap is C 'longest possible completion time' — confused; you want to SHORTEN, not lengthen.
