Trap is D 'shortest slack time' — slack means non-critical; you want zero-slack activities.

Critical path activities have ZERO SLACK — any delay there delays the project. Paying premium to compress critical-path activities is the only way to shorten the project. Other activities have slack absorbing changes already.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is assigned to audit a software development project that is more than 80 percent complete but has already overrun time by 10 percent and costs by 25 percent. Which of the following actions should the IS auditor take?

options.A: Report that the organization does not have effective project management.
options.B: Recommend that the project manager be changed.
options.D: Review the business case and project management.

questions.correct_explanation: Before making any recommendations, an information systems (IS) auditor needs to understand the project and the factors that have contributed to bringing the project over budget and over schedule.

wrong_explanations.A: The organization may have effective project management practices and still be behind schedule or over budget.
wrong_explanations.B: There is no indication that the project manager should be changed without looking into the reasons for the overrun.
wrong_explanations.C: The organization may have sound IT governance and still be behind schedule or over budget.

tips: Trap is A 'report ineffective project management' — premature conclusion without analysis.
Trap is B 'recommend changing PM' — overstep; auditor doesn't make personnel decisions.
Trap is C 'review IT governance structure' — too broad; the audit is about THIS project.
Audit response to over-budget/over-time: review business case + project management to understand WHY. Recommendations come AFTER understanding.

questions.question: During the information systems (IS) audit of large payment systems of an organization, it was noticed that during code coverage testing, the quality assurance team analyzed a nonproduction environment using logging and tracing tools. Which of the following code issues is MOST likely to be missed because of this action?

options.D: Pointer manipulation

questions.correct_explanation: The changes from a testing environment with instrumentation inserted into the code and the production environment for the code can mask timing-related issues like race conditions.

wrong_explanations.B: Bounds checking is a coding issue rather than an environmental issue.
wrong_explanations.C: Input validation is a coding issue rather than an environmental issue.
wrong_explanations.D: Pointer manipulation is a coding issue rather than an environmental issue.

tips: Trap is B 'bounds checking' — surface-detectable in either environment.
Trap is C 'input validation' — also visible in test environments.
Trap is D 'pointer manipulation' — code-readable issue, visible regardless of environment.
Race conditions are TIMING bugs. Test environments with logging/tracing tools change timing — slower, instrumented. Race conditions appear in production at full speed but hide in instrumented test.

questions.question: Which of the following system and data conversion strategies provides the GREATEST redundancy?

options.D: Parallel run

questions.correct_explanation: Parallel runs are the safest-although the most expensive-approach because both the old and new systems are run, thus incurring what might appear to be double costs.

wrong_explanations.A: Direct cutover has high risk because it does not provide for a period of testing and adjustments, nor does it provide an easy fall back option if the new system fails.
wrong_explanations.B: A pilot study approach is performed incrementally, making rollback procedures difficult to execute.
wrong_explanations.C: A phased approach is performed incrementally, making rollback procedures difficult to execute.

tips: Trap is A 'direct cutover' — least redundant; no fallback.
Trap is B 'pilot study' — partial rollout, limited redundancy.
Trap is C 'phased approach' — gradual but eventually replaces; not fully redundant.
Parallel run = both systems operate simultaneously. Maximum redundancy: if new fails, old takes over. Most expensive but safest.

questions.question: Which of the following should be developed during the requirements definition phase of a software development project to address aspects of software testing?

options.D: User acceptance test (UAT) specifications

questions.correct_explanation: A key objective in any software development project is to ensure that the developed software will meet the business objectives and the requirements of the user. The users should be involved in the requirements definition phase of a development project and user acceptance testing (UAT) specification should be developed during this phase.

wrong_explanations.A: Test data is usually created during the system testing phase.
wrong_explanations.B: Detailed test plans are created during system testing.
wrong_explanations.C: Quality assurance (QA) test specifications are set out later in the development process.

tips: Trap is A 'test data for critical applications' — operational test artifact, not requirements deliverable.
Trap is B 'detailed test plans' — operational document, downstream of requirements.
Trap is C 'QA test specifications' — also downstream of requirements.
UAT specifications belong in requirements definition because users define what they need AND how it'll be tested. Same conversation, same phase.

questions.question: At the completion of a system development project, a post-project review should include which of the following?

options.A: Assessing risk that may lead to downtime after the production release
options.B: Identifying lessons learned that may be applicable to future projects
options.C: Verifying that the controls in the delivered system are working
options.D: Ensuring that test data are deleted

questions.correct_explanation: A project team has something to learn from every project. Because risk assessment is a key issue for project management, it is important for the organization to accumulate lessons learned and integrate them into future projects.

wrong_explanations.A: An assessment of potential downtime should be made with the operations group and other specialists before implementing a system.
wrong_explanations.C: Verifying that controls are working should be covered during the acceptance test phase and possibly again in the postimplementation review. The post-project review focuses on project-related issues.
wrong_explanations.D: Test data should be retained for future regression testing.

tips: Trap is A 'assess post-release downtime risk' — ongoing concern, not post-project review.
Trap is C 'verify controls working' — pre-release activity (UAT/postimplementation).
Trap is D 'ensure test data deleted' — operational cleanup, narrow.
Post-project review = lessons learned for FUTURE projects. The point is institutional learning, not validating the current project's outcomes.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is asked to participate in project initiation meetings for a critical project. The IS auditor's MAIN concern should be that the:

options.A: complexity and risk associated with the project have been analyzed.
options.B: resources needed throughout the project have been determined.
options.D: contract for external parties involved in the project has been completed.

questions.correct_explanation: Understanding complexity and risk, and actively managing these throughout a project are critical to a successful outcome.

wrong_explanations.B: The resources needed will be dependent on the complexity of the project.
wrong_explanations.C: It is too early in the project to identify the technical deliverables.
wrong_explanations.D: Not all projects require contracts with external parties.

tips: Trap is B 'resources determined' — operational concern, addressable later.
Trap is C 'technical deliverables identified' — definition concern, secondary.
Trap is D 'external contracts complete' — administrative, secondary.
Project initiation must establish complexity and risk understanding upfront. Without that, planning is built on assumptions. Risk and complexity awareness drives every later decision.

questions.question: From a risk management point of view, the BEST approach when implementing a large and complex IT infrastructure is:

options.A: a major deployment after proof of concept.
options.C: a deployment plan based on sequenced phases.
options.D: to simulate the new infrastructure before deployment.

questions.correct_explanation: When developing a large and complex IT infrastructure, a good practice is to use a phased approach to fit the entire system together. This provides greater assurance of quality results.

wrong_explanations.A: major deployment poses a higher risk of implementation failure.
wrong_explanations.B: Prototyping may reduce development failure, but a large environment usually requires a phased approach.
wrong_explanations.D: It is not usually feasible to simulate a large and complex IT infrastructure prior to deployment.

tips: Trap is A 'major deployment after PoC' — risky; PoC doesn't validate production scale.
Trap is B 'prototyping + one-phase deployment' — combines rapid + risky deployment.
Trap is D 'simulate before deployment' — useful but doesn't replace phased rollout.
Large complex infrastructure = phased deployment. Each phase teaches the next; rollback is feasible if a phase fails. Risk distributed over time.

questions.question: When reviewing an active project, an information systems (IS) auditor observed that the business case was no longer valid because of a reduction in anticipated benefits and increased costs. The IS auditor should recommend that the:

options.B: business case be updated and possible corrective actions be identified.
options.C: project be returned to the project sponsor for re-approval.
options.D: project be completed and the business case be updated later.

questions.correct_explanation: The IS auditor should recommend that the business case be kept current throughout the project because it is a key input to decisions made throughout the life of any project.

wrong_explanations.A: An information systems (IS) auditor should not recommend discontinuing or completing the project before reviewing an updated business case.
wrong_explanations.C: The project cannot be returned to the sponsor until the business case has been updated.
wrong_explanations.D: An IS auditor should not recommend completing the project before reviewing an updated business case and ensuring approval from the project sponsor.

tips: Trap is A 'discontinue project' — drastic; analysis comes first.
Trap is C 'return to sponsor for re-approval' — bureaucratic; doesn't address the underlying problem.
Trap is D 'complete and update later' — proceeds with invalid business case; backwards.
Update business case + identify corrective actions = data-driven decision support. Lets management decide whether to continue, pivot, or stop based on current reality.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of the top-down approach to software testing?

options.B: Testing can be started before all programs are complete.
options.C: It is more effective than other testing approaches.
options.D: Errors in critical modules are detected sooner.

questions.correct_explanation: The advantage of the top-down approach is that tests of major functions are conducted early, thus enabling the detection of interface errors sooner.

wrong_explanations.B: The advantage that testing can be started before all programs are complete is characteristic of the bottom-up approach to system testing.
wrong_explanations.C: The most effective testing approach is dependent on the environment being tested.
wrong_explanations.D: Detecting errors in critical modules sooner is an advantage of the bottom-up approach to system testing.

tips: Trap is B 'testing before all programs complete' — bottom-up advantage; tests modules as ready.
Trap is C 'more effective than other approaches' — too strong; depends on context.
Trap is D 'errors in critical modules detected sooner' — that's BOTTOM-UP's specific advantage.
Top-down tests the system architecturally. Major function and interface tests run early, surfacing integration errors before deep module testing wastes effort.

questions.question: During the system testing phase of an application development project, the information systems (IS) auditor should review the:

options.D: program change requests.

questions.correct_explanation: Testing is crucial in determining that user requirements have been validated. The information systems (IS) auditor should be involved in this phase, review error reports for their precision in recognizing erroneous data and review the procedures for resolving errors.

wrong_explanations.A: A conceptual design specification is a document prepared during the requirements definition phase. The system testing is based on a test plan.
wrong_explanations.B: A vendor contract is prepared during a software acquisition process and may be reviewed to ensure that all the deliverables in the contract have been delivered, but the most important area of review is the error reports.
wrong_explanations.D: Program change requests are reviewed normally as a part of the postimplementation phase.

tips: Trap is A 'conceptual design specs' — earlier-phase artifact, not testing-phase focus.
Trap is B 'vendor contract' — administrative, not testing-phase technical concern.
Trap is D 'change requests' — process artifact, not testing focus.
Testing phase produces error reports. Auditor reviews error reports to verify: are errors being identified accurately? Is resolution happening? That's the testing-phase audit.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective recommendation for reducing the number of defects encountered during software development projects?

options.A: Increase the time allocated for system testing.
options.D: Require the sign-off of all project deliverables.

questions.correct_explanation: Inspections of code and design are a proven software quality technique. An advantage of this approach is that defects are identified before they propagate through the development life cycle. This reduces the cost of correction because less rework is involved.

wrong_explanations.A: Allowing more time for testing may discover more defects; however, little is revealed about why the quality problems are occurring, and the costs of the extra testing and rectifying the defects found will be greater than if they had been discovered earlier in the development process.
wrong_explanations.C: The ability of the development staff can have a bearing on the quality of what is produced; however, replacing staff can be expensive and disruptive, and the presence of a competent staff cannot guarantee quality in the absence of effective quality management processes.
wrong_explanations.D: Sign-off of deliverables may help detect defects if signatories are diligent about reviewing deliverable content; however, this is difficult to enforce and may occur too late in the process to be cost-effective. Deliverable reviews normally do not go down to the same level of detail as software inspections.

tips: Trap is A 'increase system testing time' — addresses symptoms, not root cause; defects propagate before reaching system test.
Trap is C 'increase development staff' — adding people doesn't reduce defects per person.
Trap is D 'sign-off on deliverables' — administrative, doesn't catch defects.
Software inspections (formal reviews) catch defects EARLY in code/design. Cheaper to fix than testing-found defects. Cost-effective per-defect-prevented.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor who is invited to a project development meeting notes that no project risk has been documented. When the IS auditor raises this issue, the project manager responds that it is too early to identify risk and that, if risk starts impacting the project, a risk manager will be hired. The appropriate response of the IS auditor is to:

options.A: stress the importance of spending time at this point in the project to consider and document risk and to develop contingency plans.
options.B: accept the project manager's position because the project manager is accountable for the outcome of the project.
options.C: offer to work with the risk manager when one is appointed.
options.D: inform the project manager that the IS auditor will conduct a review of the risk at the completion of the requirements definition phase of the project.

questions.correct_explanation: The majority of project risk can be identified before a project begins, allowing mitigation/avoidance plans to be put in place to deal with this risk, A project should have a clear link back to corporate strategy, enterprise risk management and tactical plans to support this strategy. The process ofsetting corporate strategy, setting objectives and developing tactical plans should include the consideration of risk.

wrong_explanations.B: The project manager cannot accept responsibility for risk acceptance. The risk must be addressed continuously-starting as early in the process as possible.
wrong_explanations.C: Appointing a risk manager is a good practice, but waiting until the project has been impacted by risk is misguided. Risk management needs to be forward looking; allowing risk to evolve into issues that adversely impact the project represents a failure of risk management. With or without a risk manager, people within and outside of the project team need to be consulted and encouraged to comment when they believe new risk has emerged or risk priorities have changed. The information systems (IS) auditor has an obligation to the project sponsor and the organization to advise on appropriate project management practices. Waiting for the possible appointment of a risk manager represents an unnecessary and dangerous delay in implementing risk management.
wrong_explanations.D: IS auditors cannot provide risk review without impairing their independence.

tips: Trap is B 'accept PM position' — abandons audit responsibility.
Trap is C 'wait for risk manager' — passive; risks accumulate during the wait.
Trap is D 'review risk after requirements phase' — too late; risks should be managed from the start.
Risk identification and contingency planning are CHEAPER and MORE EFFECTIVE early than late. Auditor must advocate for proactive risk management even when PM resists.

questions.question: The MAIN purpose of a transaction audit trail is to:

options.A: reduce the use of storage media.
options.B: determine accountability and responsibility for processed transactions.
options.C: help an information systems (IS) auditor trace transactions.
options.D: provide useful information for capacity planning.

questions.correct_explanation: Enabling audit trails aids in establishing the accountability and responsibility for processed transactions by tracing them through the information system.

wrong_explanations.A: Enabling audit trails increases the use of disk space.
wrong_explanations.C: A transaction log file is used to trace transactions, but the primary purpose of an audit trail is to support accountability, not to support the work of the information systems (IS) auditor.
wrong_explanations.D: The objective of capacity planning is the efficient and effective use of IT resources and requires information, such as central processing unit utilization, bandwidth and the number of users.

tips: Trap is A 'reduce storage' — opposite; audit trails INCREASE storage.
Trap is C 'help auditor trace' — useful side effect, not the main purpose.
Trap is D 'capacity planning' — operational use, not the main purpose.
Audit trails establish ACCOUNTABILITY: who did what, when. Tracing transactions through the system maps responsibility. That's the foundational purpose.

questions.question: An organization is implementing an enterprise resource planning (ERP) application. Of the following, who is PRIMARILY responsible for overseeing the project to ensure that it is progressing in accordance with the project plan and that it will deliver the expected results?

options.D: User project team

questions.correct_explanation: A project steering committee that provides an overall direction for the enterprise resource planning (ERP) implementation project is responsible for reviewing the project's progress to ensure that it will deliver the expected results.

wrong_explanations.A: A project sponsor is typically the senior manager in charge of the primary business unit that the application will support. The sponsor provides funding for the project and works closely with the project manager to define the critical success factors or metrics for the project. The project sponsor is not responsible for reviewing the progress of the project.
wrong_explanations.B: A system development project team completes the assigned tasks, works according to the instructions of the project manager and communicates with the user project team. The system development project team is not responsible for overseeing the progress of the project.
wrong_explanations.D: A user project team (UPT) completes the assigned tasks, communicates effectively with the system development team and works according to the advice of the project manager. A UPT is not responsible for reviewing the progress of the project.

tips: Trap is A 'project sponsor' — provides resources and removes obstacles, but doesn't oversee day-to-day progress.
Trap is B 'system development team' — executes, not oversees.
Trap is D 'user project team' — represents users, not project oversight.
Project steering committee = oversight body for project progress. Reviews status, approves changes, ensures alignment. Specifically designed for this responsibility.

questions.question: A legacy payroll application was migrated to a new application. Which of the following stakeholders should be PRIMARILY responsible for reviewing and signing off on the accuracy and completeness of the data before going live?

options.D: Data owner

questions.correct_explanation: During the data conversion stage of a project, the data owner is primarily responsible for reviewing and signing off that the data are migrated completely and accurately and are valid.

wrong_explanations.A: An information systems (IS) auditor should ensure that there is a review and sign-off by the data owner during the data conversion stage of the project. An IS auditor is not responsible for reviewing and signing-off on the accuracy of the converted data.
wrong_explanations.B: A database administrator's (DBA's) primary responsibility is to maintain the integrity of the database and make the database available to users. A DBA is not responsible for reviewing migrated data.
wrong_explanations.C: A project manager provides day-to-day management and leadership of the project but is not responsible for the accuracy and integrity of the data.

tips: Trap is A 'IS auditor' — independence violation; auditor can't sign off operationally.
Trap is B 'DBA' — technical role, doesn't validate business correctness of data.
Trap is C 'project manager' — manages the project, doesn't own data quality.
Data owner has the only AUTHORITY to confirm data accuracy and completeness. Going live with bad data = data owner's accountability.

questions.question: An organization is migrating from a legacy system to an enterprise resource planning system. While reviewing the data migration activity, the MOST important concern for the information systems (IS) auditor is to determine that there is a:

options.A: correlation of semantic characteristics of the data migrated between the two systems.
options.B: correlation of arithmetic characteristics of the data migrated between the two systems.
options.C: correlation of functional characteristics of the processes between the two systems.
options.D: relative efficiency of the processes between the two systems.

questions.correct_explanation: Because the two systems can have a different data representation, including the database schema, the information systems (IS) auditor's main concern should be to verify that the interpretation of the data (structure) is the same in the new system as it was in the old system.

wrong_explanations.B: Arithmetic characteristics represent aspects of data structure and internal definition in the database and, therefore, are less important than the semantic characteristics.
wrong_explanations.C: A review of the correlation of the functional characteristics between the two systems is not relevant to a data migration review.
wrong_explanations.D: A review of the relative efficiencies of the processes between the two systems is not relevant to a data migration review.

tips: Trap is B 'arithmetic characteristics' — numeric properties, but data structure matters more.
Trap is C 'functional characteristics of processes' — process concern, not data migration.
Trap is D 'process efficiency' — performance concern, not data quality.

Migration's central challenge: same data, different schema. Semantic mapping ensures meaning is preserved across schemas (a 'customer' in old system means same as 'customer' in new). Without semantic correlation, data is technically migrated but semantically broken.

questions.question: Normally, it is essential to involve which of the following stakeholders in the initiation stage of a project?

options.D: System builders

questions.correct_explanation: System owners are the information systems (project) sponsors or chief advocates. They normally are responsible for initiating and funding projects to develop, operate and maintain information systems.

wrong_explanations.B: System users are the individuals who use or are affected by the information system. Their requirements are crucial in the requirements definition, design and testing stages of a project.
wrong_explanations.C: System designers translate business requirements and constraints into technical solutions.
wrong_explanations.D: System builders construct the system based on the specifications from the systems designers. In most cases, the designers and builders are the same personnel.

tips: Trap is B 'system users' — involved later in requirements and UAT.
Trap is C 'system designers' — involved in design phase.
Trap is D 'system builders' — involved in development phase.
Initiation = funding, sponsorship, mandate. System owners (sponsors) provide all three. Without them, the project doesn't start.

questions.question: A project manager for a project that is scheduled to take 18 months to complete announces that the project is in a healthy financial position because, after six months, only one-sixth of the budget has been spent. The information systems (IS) auditor should FIRST determine:

options.A: the amount of progress achieved compared to the project schedule.
options.B: if the project budget can be reduced.
options.C: if the project can be completed ahead of schedule.
options.D: if the budget savings can be applied to increase the project scope.

questions.correct_explanation: Cost performance of a project cannot be properly assessed in isolation of schedule performance. Cost cannot be assessed simply in terms of elapsed time on a project.

wrong_explanations.B: To properly assess the project budget position, it is necessary to know how much progress has actually been made and, given this, what level of expenditure would be expected. It is possible that project expenditure appears to be low because actual progress has been slow. Until the analysis of project against schedule has been completed, it is impossible to know whether there is any reason to reduce budget. If the project has slipped behind schedule, then it is possible that not only there is no spare budget, but also extra expenditure may be needed to retrieve the slippage. The low expenditure can be representative of a situation where the project is likely to miss deadlines rather than potentially come in ahead of time.
wrong_explanations.C: If the project is found to be ahead of budget after adjusting for actual progress, this is not necessarily a good outcome, because it points to flaws in the original budgeting process; and, until further analysis is undertaken, it cannot be determined whether any spare funds actually exist.
wrong_explanations.D: If the project is behind schedule, adding scope may be the wrong thing to do.

tips: Trap is B 'reduce budget' — premature; no analysis yet.
Trap is C 'complete ahead of schedule' — premature; depends on actual progress.
Trap is D 'apply savings to scope expansion' — backwards; assumes savings without analysis.
1/6 budget at 6 months ≠ on track. Could mean: ahead of schedule, OR behind schedule and not spending. Compare progress to schedule first; cost without progress context is meaningless.

questions.question: The MAJOR advantage of a component-based development approach is the:

options.A: ability to manage an unrestricted variety of data types.
options.C: capacity to meet the demands of a changing environment.
options.D: support of multiple development environments.

questions.correct_explanation: Component-based development that relies on reusable modules can increase the speed of development. Software developers can then focus on business logic.

wrong_explanations.A: The data types must be defined within each component, and there is no certainty that any component will be able to handle multiple data types.
wrong_explanations.B: Component-based development is no better than many other development methods at modeling complex relationships.
wrong_explanations.C: Component-based development is one of the methodologies that can be effective at meeting changing requirements, but this is not its primary benefit or purpose.

tips: Trap is A 'manage unrestricted data types' — data abstraction, not the major component-based advantage.
Trap is B 'complex relationship modeling' — modeling capability, not development advantage.
Trap is C 'meet changing environment demands' — agility benefit, but not the major advantage.
Component-based development supports MULTIPLE development environments via standardized component interfaces. Components built in one environment can compose with components from others.

questions.question: The specific advantage of white box testing is that it:

options.A: verifies that a program can operate successfully with other parts of the system.
options.B: ensures a program's functional operating effectiveness without regard to the internal program structure.
options.C: determines procedural accuracy or conditions of a program's specific logic paths.
options.D: examines a program's functionality by executing it in a tightly controlled or virtual environment with restricted access to the host system.

questions.correct_explanation: White box testing assesses the effectiveness of software program logic. Specifically, test data are used in determining procedural accuracy or conditions of a program's logic paths.

wrong_explanations.A: Verifying that the program can operate successfully with other parts of the system is sociability testing.
wrong_explanations.B: Testing the program's functionality without knowledge of internal structures is black box testing.
wrong_explanations.D: Controlled testing of programs in a semidebugged environment, either heavily controlled step-by-step or via monitoring in virtual machines, is sandbox testing.

tips: Trap is A 'operates with other system parts' — that's sociability testing.
Trap is B 'functional effectiveness without internal structure' — that's BLACK box testing.
Trap is D 'tightly controlled virtual environment' — sandbox testing.
White box = code-aware testing. Tester sees the code structure and tests specific logic paths. Catches procedural errors invisible to black-box testing.

questions.question: Following good practices, formal plans for implementation of new information systems are developed during the:

options.D: deployment phase.

questions.correct_explanation: The method of implementation may affect the design of the system. Therefore, planning for implementation should begin well in advance of the actual implementation date. A formal implementation plan should be constructed in the design phase and revised as the development progresses.

wrong_explanations.A: The implementation plans are updated during the development of the system, but the plans were already addressed during the design phase.
wrong_explanations.C: The testing phase focuses on testing the system and is not concerned with implementation planning.
wrong_explanations.D: The deployment phase implements the system according to the plans set out earlier in the design phase.

tips: Trap is A 'development phase' — too late for planning; should be designed already.
Trap is C 'testing phase' — way too late.
Trap is D 'deployment phase' — much too late; implementation is happening.
Implementation method affects design (HW choices, integration points, conversion strategy). Design-phase implementation planning ensures design supports the chosen deployment approach.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing a project that is using an agile software development approach. Which of the following should the IS auditor expect to find?

options.A: Use of a capability maturity model (CMM).
options.B: Regular monitoring of task-level progress against schedule.
options.C: Extensive use of software development tools to maximize team productivity.
options.D: Post-iteration reviews that identify lessons learned for future use in the project.

questions.correct_explanation: A key tenet of the agile approach to software project management is ongoing team learning to refine project management and software development processes as the project progresses. The team considers and documents what worked well and what could have worked better at the end of each iteration and identifies improvements to be implemented in subsequent iterations. Additionally, less importance is placed on formal paper-based deliverables, with the preference being effective informal communication within the team and with key outside contributors. Agile projects produce releasable software in short iterations, typically ranging from four-to-eight weeks, which instills considerable performance discipline within the team. These practices, combined with short daily meetings to agree on what the team is doing and the identification of any impediments, render task-level tracking against a schedule redundant.

wrong_explanations.A: The capability maturity model (CMM) places heavy emphasis on predefined formal processes and formal project-management and software-development deliverables. Agile software development projects, by contrast, rely on refinement of process as dictated by the particular needs of the project and team dynamics.
wrong_explanations.B: Task-level tracking is not used because daily meetings identify challenges and impediments to the project.
wrong_explanations.C: Agile projects make use of suitable development tools; however, tools are not seen as the primary means of achieving productivity. Team harmony, effective communications and collective ability to solve challenges are of greater importance.

tips: Trap is A 'use of CMM' — process maturity model, doesn't fit agile's iterative philosophy.
Trap is B 'task-level monitoring' — agile uses outcome (sprint) monitoring, not micromanaged task tracking.
Trap is C 'extensive use of dev tools' — agile is people-and-iteration-centric, not tool-centric.
Agile's distinguishing practice: post-iteration reviews (retrospectives) where the team learns and adjusts. Continuous improvement IS agile.

questions.question: An organization sells books and music online on its secure website. Transactions are transferred to the accounting and delivery systems every hour to be processed. Which of the following controls BEST ensures that sales processed on the secure website are transferred to both systems?

options.A: Transaction totals are recorded daily in the sales systems. Daily sales system totals are aggregated and totaled.
options.B: Transactions are automatically numerically sequenced. Sequences are checked and gaps in continuity are accounted for.
options.C: Processing systems check for duplicated transaction numbers. lf a transaction number is duplicated (already present), it is rejected.
options.D: System time is synchronized hourly using a centralized time server. All transactions have a date/time stamp.

questions.correct_explanation: Automatic numerical sequencing is the only option that accounts for completeness of transactions because any missing transactions are identified by a gap.

wrong_explanations.A: Totaling transactions on the sales system does not address the transfer of data from the online systems to the accounting system, but rather considers only the sales system.
wrong_explanations.C: Checking for duplicates is a valid control; however, it does not address whether the sales transactions processed are complete ( ensuring that all transactions are recorded).
wrong_explanations.D: A date/time stamp does not help account for transactions that are missing or incomplete in the accounting and delivery systems.

tips: Trap is A 'daily totals aggregated' — detects volume mismatch but not specific transaction loss.
Trap is C 'duplicate transaction detection' — catches duplicates, not missing transactions.
Trap is D 'time stamp synchronization' — useful for correlation, doesn't ensure completeness.
Numerical sequences make GAPS visible. Missing transaction = missing sequence number = automatically detected. Best completeness control for high-volume transaction environments.

questions.question: An enterprise is developing a new procurement system that is behind schedule. As a result, the time originally planned for the test phase is proposed to be shortened. The project manager asks the information systems (IS) auditor for recommendations to mitigate the risk associated with reduced testing. Which of the following is a suitable risk mitigation strategy?

options.A: Test and release a pilot with reduced functionality.
options.B: Fix and retest the highest-severity functional defects.
options.C: Eliminate planned testing by the development team and proceed straight to acceptance testing.
options.D: Implement a test tool to automate defect tracking.

questions.correct_explanation: Testing and releasing a pilot with reduced functionality reduces risk in several ways. Reduced functionality should result in fewer test cases to run, fewer defects to fix and retest and less regression testing. A pilot release that is made available to a select group of users will reduce the risk associated with a full implementation. All of the benefits of releasing the system to the full user population will not be realized, but some benefits should start to be realized. Additionally, some useful comments from real users should be obtained to guide what extra functionality and other improvements need to be included in an entire release.

wrong_explanations.B: When testing starts, a significant number of defects are likely to exist. Focusing only on the highest­severity functional defects has the risk that other important aspects, such as usability problems and nonfunctional performance and security requirements, will be ignored. The system may go live, but users may struggle to use the system as intended to realize business benefits.
wrong_explanations.C: Eliminating testing by development is not a good solution. Before system acceptance testing begins, some prior testing should occur to establish that the system is ready to proceed to acceptance evaluation. If prior testing by development does not occur, there is a considerable risk that the software will have a significant number of low-level defects, such as transactions that cause the system to hang and unintelligible error messages. These defects can prove frustrating for users or testers tasked with acceptance testing and, ultimately, can cause the overall test time to increase rather than decrease.
wrong_explanations.D: The use of a defect tracking tool can help in improving test efficiency, but it does not address the fundamental risk caused by reducing the testing effort on a system in which quality is uncertain. Given the build problems experienced, there is reason to suspect that quality problems can exist.

tips: Trap is B 'fix highest-severity defects' — narrow scope; ignores risk that fixes break other things.
Trap is C 'eliminate dev testing, go to UAT' — bypassing dev testing creates massive UAT load and risk.
Trap is D 'automate defect tracking tool' — process improvement, doesn't reduce testing risk.
Pilot with reduced functionality limits scope of test, allowing focused testing in compressed time AND reducing user-facing risk. Can expand scope post-launch as testing catches up.
